rules.legal_concept: Right of any person to inspect, examine, and copy government records
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian must permit a government record to be inspected, examined, and copied by any person (no requester qualification beyond being a person) during regular business hours, unless the record is exempt.
rules.trigger: Any person submits a request for a government record.
rules.source_language: The custodian of a government record shall permit the record to be inspected, examined, and copied by any person during regular business hours ... unless a government record is exempt from public access.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(a) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Universal-access anchor. 'any person' is the operative eligibility term; there is no citizenship or standing qualifier at intake.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement to request records
rules.atomic_rule: Access is available to any person; OPRA imposes no residency or in-state requirement on the requestor.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional).
rules.source_language: The custodian of a government record shall permit the record to be inspected, examined, and copied by any person during regular business hours.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(a) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Universal-access symmetry rule (shared key), emitted as a rule not a negative. Source clause is verbatim; the no-residency conclusion is the settled reading of 'any person' (see Scheeler v. Atlantic County Muni. Joint Ins. Fund, 454 N.J. Super. 621 (App. Div. 2018), holding OPRA is not limited to NJ citizens) - flag for manual case verification.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required to obtain access
rules.atomic_rule: A requestor need not state a reason or purpose to obtain access; the only purpose-related field is a yes/no certification of whether the record will be used for a commercial purpose, which affects fee basis and response window (deferred), not access eligibility.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional).
rules.source_language: The form shall provide space for the name, address, email address and telephone number of the requestor and a brief description of the government record sought.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Universal-access symmetry rule (shared key). The required request fields are identity/contact and a description of the record only - no reason field. The commercial-purpose certification (NJ-A16) is the sole purpose disclosure and does not gate access, only fee/timeline treatment.

rules.legal_concept: Anonymous requests permitted; anonymity not a ground for denial
rules.atomic_rule: A request may be submitted anonymously; indicating the request is anonymous is not a ground for denial and an anonymous request is not to be considered incomplete - but an anonymous requestor may not institute an OPRA proceeding under N.J.S.A. 47:1A-6.
rules.trigger: Requestor elects to submit anonymously.
rules.source_language: A request may be submitted anonymously provided, however, that anonymous requestors shall not be permitted to institute proceedings pursuant to section 7 of P.L.2001, c.404 (C.47:1A-6). ... A request that is submitted anonymously shall not be considered incomplete.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: The loss of standing to sue is enforcement/appeal-scope (sibling); captured here only as the eligibility consequence of anonymity that the intake engine must surface.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian's response duty suspended if requestor does not accurately identify/contact
rules.atomic_rule: If the requestor has elected not to accurately identify themselves or to provide an accurate address, email address, or telephone number, the custodian is not required to respond (and the failure-to-respond deemed-denial does not run) until the requestor contacts the custodian seeking a response.
rules.trigger: Requestor provides no accurate name/address/email/telephone contact.
rules.clock_spec: tolls the custodian's response obligation indefinitely until the requestor contacts the custodian seeking a response to the original request
rules.source_language: If the requestor has elected not to accurately identify themselves or to provide an accurate address, email address, or telephone number, the custodian shall not be required to respond until the requestor contacts the custodian seeking a response to the original request.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: The underlying 7/14-business-day response deadline is Deadlines-scope (sibling); this row is the intake-identification condition that tolls it.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of custodian of a government record
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian who must receive and respond to a request is, for a municipality, the municipal clerk; for any other public agency, the officer officially designated by formal action of that agency's director or governing body.
rules.trigger: Determining who must handle a request.
rules.source_language: "Custodian of a government record" or "custodian" means in the case of a municipality, the municipal clerk and in the case of any other public agency, the officer officially designated by formal action of that agency's director or governing body, as the case may be.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-1.1 (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.1)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver (custodian designation drives routing). For municipalities the custodian is fixed by statute (municipal clerk); for other agencies the city/agency supplies the designated officer.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of government record / record
rules.atomic_rule: A requestable 'government record' is any document or information (paper, electronic, image, sound, or copy) made, maintained, kept on file, or received in the course of official business by any officer/commission/agency/authority of the State or a political subdivision, excluding inter-agency/intra-agency advisory, consultative, or deliberative material.
rules.trigger: Determining whether the requested item is subject to OPRA.
rules.source_language: "Government record" or "record" means any paper, written or printed book, document, drawing, map, plan, photograph, microfilm, data processed or image processed document, information stored or maintained electronically or by sound-recording or in a similar device, or any copy thereof, that has been made, maintained or kept on file in the course of his or its official business by any officer, commission, agency or authority of the State or of any political subdivision thereof, including subordinate boards thereof, or that has been received in the course of his or its official business by any such officer, commission, agency, or authority of the State or of any political subdivision thereof, including subordinate boards thereof. The terms shall not include inter-agency or intra-agency advisory, consultative, or deliberative material.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-1.1 (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.1)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: The deliberative-material (ACD) carve-out and the further confidential-information list are exemption/classification content handled by the Denials/Redaction sibling; captured here only as the coverage boundary of what is requestable.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of public agency / agency (includes municipalities and political subdivisions)
rules.atomic_rule: OPRA applies to any public agency, which includes any political subdivision of the State or combination of subdivisions and any division, board, bureau, office, commission, instrumentality, or independent authority within or created by a political subdivision - i.e., municipalities and their entities are covered.
rules.trigger: Determining whether the responding entity is subject to OPRA.
rules.source_language: "Public agency" or "agency" means any of the principal departments in the Executive Branch of State Government, and any division, board, bureau, office, commission or other instrumentality within or created by such department; the Legislature of the State and any office, board, bureau or commission within or created by the Legislative Branch; and any independent State authority, commission, instrumentality or agency. The terms also mean any political subdivision of the State or combination of political subdivisions, and any division, board, bureau, office, commission or other instrumentality within or created by a political subdivision of the State or combination of political subdivisions, and any independent authority, commission, instrumentality or agency created by a political subdivision or combination of political subdivisions.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-1.1 (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.1)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Establishes municipal coverage - the scope premise of the whole request-processing engine.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of commercial purpose (with excluded categories)
rules.atomic_rule: 'Commercial purpose' means the direct or indirect use of any part of a record for sale, resale, solicitation, rent, or lease of a service, or any use by which the user expects a profit through commission, salary, or fee; it excludes use by the news media, any news/journalistic/educational/scientific/scholarly/governmental organization, registered political/candidate committees, labor organizations, CBA-signatory contractors seeking enforcement information, their employees/agents/affiliates, and qualifying 501(c)(3)/(c)(4) non-profits.
rules.trigger: Classifying a request as commercial (which drives the 14-business-day response window and special-service-fee basis - both sibling-scope).
rules.source_language: "Commercial purpose" means the direct or indirect use of any part of a government record for sale, resale, solicitation, rent, or lease of a service, or any use by which the user expects a profit either through commission, salary, or fee. "Commercial purpose" shall not include the use of a government record for any purpose by: (1) the news media, or any parent company, subsidiary, or affiliate of any news media, as defined by section 2 of P.L.1977, c.253 (C.2A:84A-21a); (2) any news, journalistic, educational, scientific, scholarly, or governmental organization; (3) any person authorized to act on behalf of a candidate committee, joint candidate committee, political committee, continuing political committee, political party committee, or legislative leadership committee ... registered with the New Jersey Election Law Enforcement Commission; (4) any labor organization; (5) any contractor signatory to a collective bargaining agreement seeking information material to the enforcement of State or federal statutes or regulations regarding, but not limited to, wage and hour protections, workplace safety, or public procurement and public bidding ...; (6) any employee, agent, contractor, or affiliates of any entity identified in paragraphs (1) through (5) ...; or (7) any non-profit entity, including organizations or individuals qualified for exemption from federal taxation pursuant to section 501(c)(3) ... and section 501(c)(4) ..., when the entity does not sell, resell, solicit, rent, or lease a government record to an unaffiliated third party in a way in which the entity expects a fee.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-1.1 (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.1)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver definition the software branches on. Kept as one conjunctive row (definition + its 7 exclusion categories). The fee and 14-day-timeline consequences it triggers are Fees/Deadlines sibling-scope.

rules.legal_concept: Request must be in writing and conveyed to the appropriate custodian by an enumerated channel
rules.atomic_rule: A request for access to a government record must be in writing and hand-delivered, mailed, transmitted electronically, or otherwise conveyed to the appropriate custodian.
rules.trigger: A person initiates a records request.
rules.source_language: A request for access to a government record shall be in writing and hand-delivered, mailed, transmitted electronically, or otherwise conveyed to the appropriate custodian.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: 'appropriate custodian' ties intake to the routing rules (NJ-A06/NJ-A30).

rules.legal_concept: Custodian must adopt the GRC form; may deny an incomplete request
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian must adopt the form established by the Government Records Council for use by any person requesting a record; a request shall be submitted in the adopted form and the custodian may deny a request that is incomplete, except that indicating the request is anonymous is not a ground for denial.
rules.trigger: Custodian sets up request intake / receives a request on/off the form.
rules.source_language: The custodian of a public agency shall adopt the form established by the Government Records Council pursuant to subsection b. of section 8 of P.L.2001, c.404 (C.47:1A-7), for the use of any person who requests access to a government record held or controlled by the public agency. ... A request shall be submitted by a requestor in the form adopted by the custodian and the custodian may deny a request that is incomplete, except that a requestor indicating the request is being submitted anonymously shall not be grounds for denial.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Note: 'may deny a request that is incomplete' is discretion, not a mandatory denial.

rules.legal_concept: Required request fields (identity/contact and record description)
rules.atomic_rule: The request form must provide space for the requestor's name, address, email address, and telephone number, and a brief description of the government record sought.
rules.trigger: Composing/validating a request.
rules.source_language: The form shall provide space for the name, address, email address and telephone number of the requestor and a brief description of the government record sought.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: The 'brief description of the government record sought' is the intake-side specificity anchor for search identification (NJ-A26).

rules.legal_concept: Letter or email with all required information suffices as a valid request
rules.atomic_rule: A completed adopted form, a letter, or an email from a requestor that includes all of the information required on the adopted form suffices, in place of a completed form, as a valid government record request.
rules.trigger: Request submitted by letter or email rather than the form.
rules.source_language: A completed form adopted by the custodian, a letter, or an email from a requestor including all of the information required on the adopted form shall suffice in place of a completed form as a valid government record request.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Alternative-format equivalence to the adopted form.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian may deny a letter/email request missing required information
rules.atomic_rule: If a letter or email from a requestor does not include all of the information required on the adopted form, the custodian may deny the record request.
rules.trigger: Letter/email request lacks required form information.
rules.source_language: If a letter or an email from a requestor does not include all of the information required on the adopted form, the custodian may deny the record request.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Discretionary denial ('may'), not mandatory.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian may deny where a letter/email has excessive information requiring more than reasonable effort to clarify
rules.atomic_rule: If a letter or email from a requestor includes substantially more information than required on the adopted form and requires more than reasonable effort to clarify the information, the custodian may deny the request.
rules.trigger: Request contains substantially more information than required and clarifying it would take more than reasonable effort.
rules.source_language: If the letter or email from a requestor includes substantially more information than required on the adopted form and requires more than reasonable effort to clarify the information, the custodian may deny the request.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: 'more than reasonable effort to clarify' is a soft standard; the statute permits denial rather than requiring a clarification exchange (no mandatory cure/clarification clock exists - see material negative).

rules.legal_concept: Requestor must certify commercial vs non-commercial use for the request to be fulfilled
rules.atomic_rule: The form must include space for the requestor to certify whether the record will be used by the requestor or another person for a commercial purpose, and the requestor is required to provide this information for the request to be fulfilled.
rules.trigger: Any request; certification is a fulfillment precondition.
rules.source_language: The form also shall include space for a requestor to certify whether the government record will be used by that requestor or another person for a commercial purpose, and the requestor shall be required to provide this information for the request to be fulfilled.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Feeds the commercial-purpose classification (NJ-A09) that drives the 14-business-day window and special fee (sibling).

rules.legal_concept: Each submission must be made to the custodian of not more than one public agency
rules.atomic_rule: Each submission of a government record request form or email record request must be made to the custodian of not more than one public agency.
rules.trigger: Requestor submits a request.
rules.source_language: Each submission of a government record request form or an email record request shall be made to the custodian of not more than one public agency.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: One-agency-per-submission constraint at intake.

rules.legal_concept: Repeated requests to multiple custodians in the same agency while one is pending may be denied
rules.atomic_rule: Submission of repeated requests to multiple custodians in the same public agency for the same record, while an identical or substantially similar request is pending in the agency, permits the custodian to deny the request.
rules.trigger: Same/substantially similar request already pending in the agency and requestor sends it to multiple custodians.
rules.source_language: Submission of repeated requests to multiple custodians in the same public agency for the same record, while an identical or substantially similar request is pending in the agency, shall permit the custodian to deny the request.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Discretionary denial for duplicative pending requests.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian need not complete an identical repeat request when information is unchanged
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian is not required to complete an identical request for a record from the same requestor if the information has not changed; but this does not prevent periodic requests regarding regularly updated records (e.g., certified payrolls, permits, licensing applications).
rules.trigger: Same requestor resubmits an identical request and the record is unchanged.
rules.source_language: The custodian shall not be required to complete an identical request for access to a government record from the same requestor if the information has not changed. Nothing in this section shall prevent a requestor from filing periodic requests regarding regularly updated public records, including, but not limited to, certified payrolls, permits, and licensing applications.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Kept as one row: the exception (periodic requests for regularly-updated records) is a proviso to the same rule.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic/online portal and fax submission permitted
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency may make available on its website an online form, portal, or software for transmitting requests electronically, and the GRC form may be submitted electronically or by fax.
rules.trigger: Agency offers electronic intake; requestor submits electronically or by fax.
rules.source_language: A public agency may make available to the public on its website an online form, portal, or software for transmitting requests electronically. The form established by the Government Records Council, pursuant to subsection b. of section 8 of P.L.2001, c.404 (C.47:1A-7), may be submitted electronically or by fax.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Permissive electronic-intake channel; agency option, not mandatory.

rules.legal_concept: Custodians with electronic forms must post submission directions on the website
rules.atomic_rule: Custodians who have adopted electronic government record request forms must provide directions on how to submit requests, including any required forms, on the public agency's website.
rules.trigger: Agency has adopted an electronic request form.
rules.source_language: Custodians who have adopted electronic government record request forms shall provide directions on how to submit requests for government records, including any required forms, on the public agency's website.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Conditional on the agency having adopted electronic forms.

rules.legal_concept: Requestor must certify whether the record is sought in connection with a legal proceeding
rules.atomic_rule: The requestor is required to certify whether the government record is being sought in connection with a legal proceeding and identify the proceeding, for the request to be fulfilled.
rules.trigger: Any request; certification is a fulfillment precondition.
rules.source_language: The requestor shall be required to certify whether the government record is being sought in connection with a legal proceeding and identify the proceeding for the request to be fulfilled.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Mandatory certification feeding the legal-proceeding bar (NJ-A23).

rules.legal_concept: Party to a legal proceeding may not use OPRA for a record subject to a court order/pending discovery
rules.atomic_rule: A party to a legal proceeding may not request a government record if the record sought is the subject of a court order including a pending discovery request, and the custodian is not required to complete such a request.
rules.trigger: Requestor is a party (or its attorney/agent) to a legal proceeding and the record is subject of a court order or pending discovery in that proceeding.
rules.source_language: A party to a legal proceeding may not request a government record if the record sought is the subject of a court order including a pending discovery request, and a custodian shall not be required to complete such a request. ... For purposes of this provision, a party to a legal proceeding shall include a party subject to a court order, any attorney representing that party, and any person acting as an agent for or on behalf of that party.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Statute preserves a carve-out: this does not bar a request by a labor organization or CBA-signatory contractor seeking information material to enforcement of wage/hour, workplace-safety, or public-procurement statutes when not sought in furtherance of discovery. Flag for human legal review before automating the bar.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian must attempt a reasonable solution before denying a request that would substantially disrupt operations
rules.atomic_rule: If a request would substantially disrupt agency operations, the custodian may deny access only after informing the requestor of the potential disruption and attempting to reach a reasonable solution with the requestor that accommodates the interests of both the requestor and the agency.
rules.trigger: Fulfilling the request would substantially disrupt agency operations.
rules.source_language: If a request for access to a government record would substantially disrupt agency operations, the custodian may deny access to the record after informing the requestor of the potential disruption to agency operations and attempting to reach a reasonable solution with the requestor that accommodates the interests of the requestor and the agency.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: The closest OPRA analog to a mandatory clarification/negotiation step, but it is conditioned on substantial disruption, not on request ambiguity. 'reasonable solution' / 'substantially disrupt' are soft standards; no numeric threshold.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian need not perform research or create new records
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian is not required to complete a request if the custodian determines that the request would require research and the collection of information from the contents of government records and the creation of new government records setting forth that research and information.
rules.trigger: Request would require research/collection and creation of a new record.
rules.source_language: A custodian shall not be required to complete a request ... if the custodian determines that the request would require research and the collection of information from the contents of government records and the creation of new government records setting forth that research and information.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Codifies the long-standing OPRA rule that a request must seek identifiable records, not compel research/analysis.

rules.legal_concept: Correspondence-type requests must specify accounts/subject/time period
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian is not required to complete a request for mail, email, text messages, correspondence, or social media postings/messages unless the request identifies a specific job title or accounts to be searched, a specific subject matter, and is confined to a reasonable time period.
rules.trigger: Request seeks correspondence-type records (mail/email/text/social media).
rules.source_language: A custodian shall not be required to complete a request including for, but not limited to, mail, email, text messages, correspondence, or social media postings and messages, if the request does not identify a specific job title or accounts to be searched, a specific subject matter, and is not confined to a reasonable time period.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: 'reasonable time period' is a soft standard bounding the search's date range (not a processing clock). Three conjunctive requirements: (1) job title or accounts, (2) subject matter, (3) reasonable time period.

rules.legal_concept: Identifying custodians/individuals by job title and position suffices for a search
rules.atomic_rule: It is sufficient for a requestor to identify specific individuals to be searched by the individual's job title and position.
rules.trigger: Requestor identifies the accounts/individuals to search.
rules.source_language: It shall be sufficient for a requestor to identify specific individuals by the individual's job title and position.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Companion/proviso to NJ-A26 - a requestor need not name the individual, only the job title/position.

rules.legal_concept: Mode of access: inspect, examine, and copy during regular business hours
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian must permit a non-exempt government record to be inspected, examined, and copied during regular business hours.
rules.trigger: A valid request for a non-exempt record.
rules.source_language: The custodian of a government record shall permit the record to be inspected, examined, and copied by any person during regular business hours.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(a) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Split from NJ-A01: this row captures the access mode (inspect/examine/copy) and timing (regular business hours); NJ-A01 captures the 'any person' eligibility. Pre-access redaction of SSN/CC/phone/DL is Redaction-scope (sibling).

rules.legal_concept: Minimum inspection hours for small municipalities, small boards of education, and small public authorities
rules.atomic_rule: For a municipality with population 5,000 or fewer (most recent federal decennial census), a board of education with total district enrollment 500 or fewer, or a public authority with less than $10 million in assets, records access must be available during not less than six regular business hours over not less than three business days per week, or the entity's regularly-scheduled business hours, whichever is less.
rules.trigger: Responding entity is a qualifying small municipality, small board of education, or small public authority.
rules.clock_spec: floor: not less than 6 regular business hours over not less than 3 business days per week (or the entity's regular hours, whichever is less)
rules.source_language: or in the case of a municipality having a population of 5,000 or fewer according to the most recent federal decennial census, a board of education having a total district enrollment of 500 or fewer, or a public authority having less than $10 million in assets, during not less than six regular business hours over not less than three business days per week or the entity's regularly-scheduled business hours, whichever is less
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(a) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Parameter with a floor (minimum access hours) and eligibility thresholds (pop 5,000 / enrollment 500 / $10M assets). 'whichever is less' caps the floor at the entity's own regular hours for very-limited-hours entities.

rules.legal_concept: Any employee receiving a request must forward it to, or direct the requestor to, the custodian
rules.atomic_rule: Any officer or employee of a public agency who receives a request for access to a government record must forward the request to the custodian of the record or direct the requestor to the custodian of the record.
rules.trigger: A request is received by a non-custodian officer/employee.
rules.source_language: Any officer or employee of a public agency who receives a request for access to a government record shall forward the request to the custodian of the record or direct the requestor to the custodian of the record.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(h) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: wrong-department routing to the correct custodian.

rules.legal_concept: Request not considered submitted until received by the custodian
rules.atomic_rule: A request is not considered submitted until it is received by the custodian of records.
rules.trigger: Request delivered to a non-custodian and forwarded/redirected.
rules.source_language: The request shall not be considered submitted until it is received by the custodian of records.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(h) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Defines the clock-start event (receipt by custodian) for the response deadline that the Deadlines sibling computes; clock_effect marked none because this row defines the start reference, it does not itself set/run a deadline.

rules.legal_concept: Agency not in possession of another agency's courtesy-copy/remote-access record
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency is not considered to be in possession of a record created, maintained, or received by another public agency and made available only by remote access to a computer network or by distribution as a courtesy copy (unless the originating agency resides within the judicial branch), and a custodian receiving a request for such a record is not obligated to provide it.
rules.trigger: Requested record was created/maintained/received by another agency and is present only via remote access or courtesy copy.
rules.source_language: A public agency shall not be considered to be in possession of a public record that is created, maintained, or received by another public agency and made available to the public agency either by remote access to a computer network or by distribution as a courtesy copy, unless the agency that created, maintained, or received the record resides within the judicial branch of the State Government. A records custodian of a public agency that receives a request for a record created, maintained, or received by another public agency, shall not be obligated to provide the record to the requestor.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Coverage/possession boundary that governs routing; paired with the referral duty NJ-A33.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian must refer requestor to the originating agency within seven business days
rules.atomic_rule: If the custodian does not provide a record held only by another agency, the custodian must direct the requestor, within seven business days, to the public agency that (to the best of their knowledge) created, maintains, or received the record; at which time the request is considered completed.
rules.trigger: Custodian declines to provide an out-of-possession record (per NJ-A32).
rules.clock_spec: 7 business days from receipt of the request to direct the requestor to the originating agency; request then deemed completed (terminal)
rules.source_language: In the event the custodian does not provide the record, the custodian shall direct the requestor within seven business days to the public agency that, to the best of their knowledge, created, maintains, or received the requested record, at which time the request shall be considered completed.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Routing path with an intrinsic 7-business-day referral deadline and a terminal outcome (request considered completed). Captured here because the referral is a Custody/Routing fork; the terminal completion also interests the Deadlines sibling.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian may redirect requestor to a record readily available on the agency website
rules.atomic_rule: If a government record in complete and unabridged form is readily available on the public agency's website, the custodian may require the requestor to obtain it from the website (which must contain a search-bar feature on its home page), and the custodian must provide directions to assist in finding the record, including the website URL and the on-site location (search bar, menu, tab, link, landing page).
rules.trigger: Requested record is readily available, complete and unabridged, on the agency website.
rules.source_language: If the government record in a complete and unabridged form is readily available on a public agency's website, the custodian may require the requestor to obtain the record from the website, which shall contain a search bar feature on its home page. The custodian shall provide the requestor with directions to assist in finding the record on the website, including providing the website URL address and the location on the website of the search bar, menu button, tab, link, landing page or equivalent, which contains the requested record.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(e) (as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2)
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by P.L.2024, c.16, eff. Sept. 3, 2024)
rules.notes: Routing-to-self-service fork. Follow-on rules deferred to siblings: the 7-business-day 'deemed fulfilled' clock if the requestor does not respond, the 7-day custodian-assist duty, and the physical-copy fallback at a fee not exceeding twice production cost (Deadlines/Fees scope). Also in this subsection but deferred: immediate-access categories (budgets/bills/vouchers/contracts/salary) and the 24-month immediate-access limit are Production/Deadlines scope.

rules.legal_concept: Time period for custodian's response (grant or deny)
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall grant access to, or deny, a government-record request as soon as possible but not later than seven business days after receiving the request, provided the record is currently available and not in storage or archived.
rules.trigger: Custodian receives a request for a currently-available record
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from request receipt (ceiling; 'as soon as possible' soft floor overlay)
rules.source_language: Unless a shorter time period is otherwise provided by statute, regulation, or executive order, a custodian of a government record shall grant access to a government record or deny a request for access to a government record as soon as possible, but not later than seven business days after receiving the request, ... provided that the record is currently available and not in storage or archived.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Core response duty and default clock. 'as soon as possible' is a soft floor; seven business days is the hard ceiling. Clock start defined by NJ-T25 (received by custodian).

rules.legal_concept: Extended 14-business-day window for commercial-purpose requests
rules.atomic_rule: The response window is not later than 14 business days if the request is for a commercial purpose.
rules.trigger: Request certified/identified as being for a commercial purpose
rules.clock_spec: 14 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: a custodian of a government record shall grant access to a government record or deny a request for access to a government record as soon as possible, but not later than seven business days after receiving the request, or 14 business days if the request is for a commercial purpose ... but the custodian shall notify the requestor of the additional response time within seven business days
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: 'Commercial purpose' defined at NJ-T47. Additional-time notice within 7 business days is NJ-T04.

rules.legal_concept: Extended 14-business-day window for covered-officer privacy review
rules.atomic_rule: The response window is not later than 14 business days if the records must be reviewed by the agency for compliance with P.L.2021, c.371 (covered-officer home-address protection).
rules.trigger: Records must be reviewed for P.L.2021 c.371 compliance
rules.clock_spec: 14 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: or 14 business days if the request is for a commercial purpose or if the records have to be reviewed by the public agency for the purpose of the agency's compliance with P.L.2021, c.371 (C.47:1B-1 et seq.), but the custodian shall notify the requestor of the additional response time within seven business days
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Same 14-day window as commercial requests but triggered by covered-officer redaction review (see NJ-T36).

rules.legal_concept: Notice of additional response time
rules.atomic_rule: When invoking the 14-business-day window (commercial or c.371 review), the custodian shall notify the requestor of the additional response time within seven business days.
rules.trigger: Custodian invokes the 14-business-day extended window
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: but the custodian shall notify the requestor of the additional response time within seven business days
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Required notice step; the 7-business-day timing is the configurable value within the notice fork.

rules.legal_concept: Additional seven business days for small fire districts
rules.atomic_rule: The seven- or fourteen-business-day response periods are an additional seven business days longer if the public agency is a fire district employing one or fewer full-time employees serving as custodians.
rules.trigger: Agency is a fire district with one or fewer full-time custodian-employees
rules.clock_spec: +7 business-days added to the applicable 7- or 14-business-day window
rules.source_language: The response time periods of seven or 14 business days, as established in this subsection, shall be an additional seven business days longer if the public agency is a fire district which employs one or fewer full-time employees who serve as custodians.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Agency-attribute-driven fixed extension.

rules.legal_concept: Commercial requestor expedite to seven business days
rules.atomic_rule: If a commercial requestor wishes to receive the record within seven business days, the custodian shall provide a copy and may charge a special service fee not exceeding two times the cost of production.
rules.trigger: Commercial requestor elects seven-business-day delivery
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from request receipt (elected expedite)
rules.source_language: If a commercial requestor would like to receive the record within seven business days, as established in this subsection, the custodian shall provide the requestor with a copy of the record and may charge a special service fee not exceeding two times the cost of the production of the record.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Expedite path is in-scope (Production/Deadlines); the '2x cost' fee ceiling belongs to the Fees sibling agent.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable extension for unforeseen circumstances
rules.atomic_rule: If unable to fulfill a request due to unforeseen circumstances or circumstances reasonably necessitating more time, the custodian is entitled to a reasonable extension of any response deadline.
rules.trigger: Unforeseen circumstances reasonably necessitating additional time
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: 'reasonable extension' of the response deadline
rules.source_language: In the event a records custodian is unable to fulfill a records request due to unforeseen circumstances or circumstances that otherwise reasonably necessitate additional time to fulfill the records request, the custodian shall be entitled to a reasonable extension of any response deadline and shall notify the requestor of the time extension within seven business days after receiving the request.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Soft-standard 'reasonable' extension; do not convert to a fixed day-count. Paired notice duty split to NJ-T08.

rules.legal_concept: Notice of time extension
rules.atomic_rule: When taking a reasonable extension for unforeseen circumstances, the custodian shall notify the requestor of the time extension within seven business days after receiving the request.
rules.trigger: Custodian invokes an unforeseen-circumstances extension
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: the custodian shall be entitled to a reasonable extension of any response deadline and shall notify the requestor of the time extension within seven business days after receiving the request.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Distinct from NJ-T04 (which is the commercial/c.371 additional-time notice).

rules.legal_concept: Deemed denial upon failure to respond
rules.atomic_rule: Failure of the custodian to respond within the applicable seven or fourteen business days is deemed a denial of the request (unless the requestor elected not to accurately identify themselves or provide accurate contact information).
rules.trigger: No custodian response by the applicable 7- or 14-business-day deadline
rules.clock_spec: terminal event at expiry of 7 or 14 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: In the event a custodian fails to respond within seven business days or 14 business days, as appropriate, after receiving a request, the failure to respond shall be deemed a denial of the request, unless the requestor has elected not to accurately identify themselves or to provide an accurate address, email address, or telephone number.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver deemed/constructive-denial trigger; remedy amounts (attorney fees/penalties) are excluded and belong to Enforcement sibling.

rules.legal_concept: Suspension of response duty for inaccurately-identified requestor
rules.atomic_rule: If the requestor elected not to accurately identify themselves or to provide an accurate address, email, or telephone number, the custodian is not required to respond until the requestor contacts the custodian seeking a response to the original request.
rules.trigger: Requestor declined to accurately identify or provide accurate contact info
rules.clock_spec: response clock does not run until requestor contacts custodian
rules.source_language: If the requestor has elected not to accurately identify themselves or to provide an accurate address, email address, or telephone number, the custodian shall not be required to respond until the requestor contacts the custodian seeking a response to the original request.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Also disables the deemed-denial trigger (NJ-T09) for such requestors.

rules.legal_concept: Advisement that record is in storage or archived
rules.atomic_rule: If the record is in storage or archived, the custodian shall so advise the requestor within seven or fourteen business days (as appropriate) after receiving the request, and advise when the record can be made available.
rules.trigger: Requested record is in storage or archived
rules.clock_spec: 7 or 14 business-days from request receipt to advise
rules.source_language: If the government record is in storage or archived, the requestor shall be so advised within seven or 14 business days, as appropriate, after the custodian receives the request. The requestor shall be advised by the custodian when the record can be made available, which shall be no more than 21 business days from the date the requestor is so advised.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Entry point of the storage/archived processing path.

rules.legal_concept: Maximum time to make stored/archived record available
rules.atomic_rule: A stored or archived record must be made available no more than 21 business days from the date the requestor is advised it is in storage/archived.
rules.trigger: Custodian has advised requestor the record is in storage/archived
rules.clock_spec: 21 business-days from date requestor is advised
rules.source_language: The requestor shall be advised by the custodian when the record can be made available, which shall be no more than 21 business days from the date the requestor is so advised.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Ceiling on the storage-path production window.

rules.legal_concept: Deemed denial if stored/archived record not timely produced
rules.atomic_rule: If a stored/archived record is not made available by the advised availability time (max 21 business days), access shall be deemed denied.
rules.trigger: Stored/archived record not made available by the advised deadline
rules.clock_spec: terminal event at expiry of the storage-availability window (<=21 business-days)
rules.source_language: If the record is not made available by that time, access shall be deemed denied.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Terminal event for the storage path.

rules.legal_concept: Requestor window to retrieve completed records
rules.atomic_rule: A requestor shall have 14 business days to retrieve the government records following the custodian's notice that the request is completed and the records are available.
rules.trigger: Custodian notifies requestor the request is completed and records available
rules.clock_spec: 14 business-days from completion/availability notice
rules.source_language: A requestor shall have 14 business days to retrieve the government records following notice from the custodian that the request has been completed and the records are available.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Requestor-side pickup window (fixed grant to requestor).

rules.legal_concept: Suspension of response deadlines during declared emergency
rules.atomic_rule: During a declared state of emergency, public health emergency, or state of local disaster emergency, the response deadlines under (i)(1) and subsection e. do not apply, but the custodian shall make a reasonable effort to respond within 7 or 14 business days, or as soon as possible thereafter.
rules.trigger: Declared state of emergency / public health emergency / local disaster emergency
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: statutory deadlines do not apply; 'reasonable effort ... as soon as possible' from request receipt
rules.source_language: During a period declared pursuant to the laws of this State as a state of emergency, public health emergency, or state of local disaster emergency, the deadlines by which to respond to a request for, or grant or deny access to, a government record under paragraph (1) of this subsection or subsection e. of this section shall not apply, provided, however, that the custodian of a government record shall make a reasonable effort, as the circumstances permit, to respond to a request for access to a government record within seven business days or 14 business days, as appropriate, or as soon as possible thereafter.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(2), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Tolls both the (i)(1) response clock and the subsection-e immediate-access requirement.

rules.legal_concept: Redirect to agency that created/maintains the record
rules.atomic_rule: For a record created/maintained/received by another agency and made available only by remote access or courtesy copy (unless that agency is in the judicial branch), the custodian is not obligated to produce it and, if not providing it, shall direct the requestor within seven business days to the originating agency, at which time the request is considered completed.
rules.trigger: Requested record was created/maintained/received by another non-judicial-branch agency and made available only via remote access or courtesy copy
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from request receipt to redirect; redirect completes the request (terminal)
rules.source_language: A public agency shall not be considered to be in possession of a public record that is created, maintained, or received by another public agency and made available to the public agency either by remote access to a computer network or by distribution as a courtesy copy, unless the agency that created, maintained, or received the record resides within the judicial branch of the State Government. A records custodian of a public agency that receives a request for a record created, maintained, or received by another public agency, shall not be obligated to provide the record to the requestor. In the event the custodian does not provide the record, the custodian shall direct the requestor within seven business days to the public agency that, to the best of their knowledge, created, maintains, or received the requested record, at which time the request shall be considered completed.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Routing keeper-sliver; also a terminal completion event on redirect.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to complete unchanged identical repeat request
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian is not required to complete an identical request for access from the same requestor if the information has not changed.
rules.trigger: Same requestor submits an identical request and the information has not changed
rules.source_language: The custodian shall not be required to complete an identical request for access to a government record from the same requestor if the information has not changed.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Limited by the periodic-request carve-out (NJ-T18).

rules.legal_concept: Periodic requests for regularly-updated records permitted
rules.atomic_rule: Nothing prevents a requestor from filing periodic requests regarding regularly updated public records, including certified payrolls, permits, and licensing applications.
rules.trigger: Requestor files periodic requests for regularly-updated records
rules.source_language: Nothing in this section shall prevent a requestor from filing periodic requests regarding regularly updated public records, including, but not limited to, certified payrolls, permits, and licensing applications.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Carve-out to the identical-request limitation.

rules.legal_concept: Prompt compliance with request
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall promptly comply with a request to inspect, examine, copy, or provide a copy of a government record.
rules.trigger: Custodian receives a valid request
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: 'promptly' from request receipt
rules.source_language: A custodian shall promptly comply with a request to inspect, examine, copy, or provide a copy of a government record.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Soft 'promptly' standard operating alongside the seven-business-day ceiling (NJ-T01).

rules.legal_concept: Notice of specific basis when unable to comply
rules.atomic_rule: If unable to comply with a request, the custodian shall indicate the specific basis on the request form, promptly return it to the requestor, and sign and date the form and provide the requestor a copy.
rules.trigger: Custodian is unable to comply with a request for access
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: 'promptly' return of the form
rules.source_language: If the custodian is unable to comply with a request for access, the custodian shall indicate the specific basis therefor on the request form and promptly return it to the requestor. The custodian shall sign and date the form and provide the requestor with a copy thereof.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Denial reason-statement notice; the denial-remedy/appeal itself is a sibling (Denials/Appeals) area.

rules.legal_concept: Denial for substantial disruption after notice and attempted solution
rules.atomic_rule: If a request would substantially disrupt agency operations, the custodian may deny access after informing the requestor of the potential disruption and attempting to reach a reasonable solution accommodating both parties' interests.
rules.trigger: Request would substantially disrupt agency operations
rules.source_language: If a request for access to a government record would substantially disrupt agency operations, the custodian may deny access to the record after informing the requestor of the potential disruption to agency operations and attempting to reach a reasonable solution with the requestor that accommodates the interests of the requestor and the agency.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: In-scope for the mandatory communication step (inform + attempt solution) preceding any denial.

rules.legal_concept: Explanation and itemized list of special service fees
rules.atomic_rule: When imposing a special service charge, the custodian shall provide the requestor with an explanation for, and an itemized list of, the fees or charges.
rules.trigger: Custodian imposes a special service charge
rules.source_language: The custodian shall provide the requestor with an explanation for and an itemized list of the fees or charges.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(c), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Communication duty is in-scope; the underlying special-service-charge amount/basis belongs to the Fees sibling.

rules.legal_concept: Opportunity to review and object to fees before incurred
rules.atomic_rule: The requestor shall have the opportunity to review and object to any fee or charge prior to it being incurred; there is a rebuttable presumption fees are reasonable, and on objection the burden is on the requestor to show they are unreasonable.
rules.trigger: A fee or charge is to be imposed on a request
rules.source_language: The requestor shall have the opportunity to review and object to any fee or charge prior to it being incurred. There shall be a rebuttable presumption that the fees or charges presented by the custodian are reasonable. If the requestor objects to the fees or charges, the burden of proof shall be on the requestor to demonstrate that the fees or charges are unreasonable.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(c), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Pre-charge review-and-object communication step plus reasonableness presumption/burden.

rules.legal_concept: Publication of appeal rights on website and request form
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall include, on the agency's website and public-records request form, information regarding a requestor's right to appeal a denial of or failure to provide access and the appeal procedure, including the GRC's website address and toll-free information line phone number.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing obligation)
rules.source_language: A custodian shall include information on the public agency's website and public records request form regarding a requestor's right to appeal a denial of, or failure to provide, access to a government record and the procedure by which an appeal may be filed, which shall include the website address and toll-free information line phone number of the Government Records Council.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(j), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: 2024 amendment replaced the prior physical-posting requirement with website/form publication.

rules.legal_concept: Forwarding request to custodian; receipt defines submission
rules.atomic_rule: Any officer or employee who receives a records request shall forward it to, or direct the requestor to, the custodian; the request is not considered submitted until received by the custodian of records.
rules.trigger: An officer or employee other than the custodian receives a request
rules.source_language: Any officer or employee of a public agency who receives a request for access to a government record shall forward the request to the custodian of the record or direct the requestor to the custodian of the record. The request shall not be considered submitted until it is received by the custodian of records.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(h), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Wrong-department routing keeper-sliver; second sentence defines the clock-start event for NJ-T01 (receipt by custodian).

rules.legal_concept: Access in requested medium/format if maintained
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall permit access and provide a copy in the medium or format requested if the agency maintains the record in that medium or format.
rules.trigger: Requestor specifies a medium/format the agency maintains
rules.source_language: A custodian shall permit access to a government record and provide a copy thereof in the medium or format requested if the public agency maintains the record in that medium or format.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(d), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2

rules.legal_concept: Conversion to requested format when available
rules.atomic_rule: If the agency does not maintain the record in the requested medium/format, the custodian shall convert it to the requested medium/format if that medium/format is available to the agency and does not require a substantial amount of manipulation or programming of information technology or the services of a third-party vendor.
rules.trigger: Requested medium/format not maintained but available without substantial IT manipulation
rules.source_language: If the public agency does not maintain the record in the medium or format requested, the custodian shall convert the record to the medium or format requested, if the medium or format is available to the public agency and does not require a substantial amount of manipulation or programming of information technology, or the services of a third party vendor.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(d), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: The conversion special-service-fee (labor/IT cost) belongs to the Fees sibling.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to convert electronic format requiring substantial manipulation
rules.atomic_rule: If the agency does not maintain the record in the requested electronic medium/format and it is not available without substantial IT manipulation or programming, the custodian need not convert it but shall at minimum provide a copy in the electronic format maintained by the agency.
rules.trigger: Requested electronic format unavailable without substantial IT manipulation
rules.source_language: If the public agency does not maintain the record in the electronic medium or format requested, and the medium or format is not available to the public agency without a substantial amount of manipulation or programming of information technology, the custodian shall be under no obligation to convert the record to the electronic medium or format requested but shall, at a minimum, provide a copy in the electronic format maintained by the public agency.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(d), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Fallback-format production floor.

rules.legal_concept: Immediate access record categories
rules.atomic_rule: Immediate access ordinarily shall be granted to budgets, bills, vouchers, contracts (including collective negotiations agreements and individual employment contracts), and public employee salary and overtime information.
rules.trigger: Request for one of the enumerated immediate-access record categories
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: 'immediate access' from request receipt
rules.source_language: Immediate access ordinarily shall be granted to budgets, bills, vouchers, contracts, including collective negotiations agreements and individual employment contracts, and public employee salary and overtime information.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(e), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Special expedited category; 'immediate' is a soft standard, tolled during declared emergencies (NJ-T15).

rules.legal_concept: Immediate access not required for records over 24 months old
rules.atomic_rule: Immediate access to government records is not required to be granted for documents over 24 months old.
rules.trigger: Requested immediate-access document is more than 24 months old
rules.source_language: Immediate access to government records shall not be required to be granted for documents over 24 months old.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(e), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: 2024 amendment raised the threshold from 12 to 24 months. Age threshold is the configurable value.

rules.legal_concept: Redirect requestor to record available on agency website
rules.atomic_rule: If the government record in complete and unabridged form is readily available on the agency's website (which must have a home-page search bar), the custodian may require the requestor to obtain it from the website and shall provide directions (URL and location of the search bar/menu/tab/link/landing page) to find it.
rules.trigger: Requested record available complete and unabridged on the agency website
rules.source_language: If the government record in a complete and unabridged form is readily available on a public agency's website, the custodian may require the requestor to obtain the record from the website, which shall contain a search bar feature on its home page. The custodian shall provide the requestor with directions to assist in finding the record on the website, including providing the website URL address and the location on the website of the search bar, menu button, tab, link, landing page or equivalent, which contains the requested record.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(e), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Entry point of the website-fulfillment path (NJ-T32 through NJ-T34).

rules.legal_concept: Website request deemed fulfilled after seven business days
rules.atomic_rule: If the requestor does not respond within seven business days of the custodian providing website information, the request is deemed fulfilled, unless the website version omits non-protected information in the original, in which case the custodian shall produce the original subject to required redactions.
rules.trigger: Requestor does not respond within seven business days of website-location notice
rules.clock_spec: terminal (deemed fulfilled) at 7 business-days from custodian providing website info
rules.source_language: If the requestor does not respond to the custodian within seven business days of the custodian providing information about a record on the public agency's website, the request shall be deemed fulfilled unless the version of the government record on the public agency's website fails to contain non-protected information contained in the original record, in which case the custodian shall produce the original version of the record subject to any redactions required by law.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(e), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Terminal fulfillment event with a completeness carve-back to original-record production.

rules.legal_concept: Website location assistance on good-faith failure
rules.atomic_rule: If the requestor cannot find the record after a good-faith effort, the requestor shall notify the custodian within seven business days, and the custodian shall make a reasonable attempt to assist within seven business days of that notification.
rules.trigger: Requestor unable to locate record on website after good-faith effort
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days for requestor to notify; 7 business-days for custodian to assist
rules.source_language: If, after the custodian has provided instructions on how to find a record on a public agency's website, the requestor is unable to find the record upon making a good faith effort to locate the record on the website, the requestor shall notify the custodian within seven business days of the custodian providing the information. Upon receiving such a request for assistance from a requestor, the custodian shall make a reasonable attempt to assist the requestor in finding the record on the website within seven business days of the requestor notifying the custodian.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(e), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Two paired seven-business-day windows in the website path.

rules.legal_concept: Physical copy when website record cannot be located
rules.atomic_rule: If the requestor is still unable to locate the record and requests a physical copy, the custodian shall provide a physical copy within seven business days of the request for a physical copy, for a fee not exceeding two times the cost of production.
rules.trigger: Requestor still cannot locate the website record and requests a physical copy
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from the request for a physical copy
rules.source_language: If the requestor is still unable to locate the record and requests a physical copy, the custodian shall provide the requestor with a physical copy of the record, for a fee not exceeding two times the cost of the production of the document. The custodian shall provide the requestor with the physical copy of the record within seven business days of the request for a physical copy.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(e), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Production step; the '2x cost' fee ceiling belongs to the Fees sibling.

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory redaction of personal identifiers
rules.atomic_rule: Prior to allowing access to any record, the custodian shall redact any information disclosing the social security number, credit card number, personal telephone number, or driver license number of any person (subject to enumerated government-use and child-support exceptions).
rules.trigger: Record to be disclosed contains SSN, credit card, personal telephone, or driver license number
rules.source_language: Prior to allowing access to any government record, the custodian thereof shall redact from that record any information which discloses the social security number, credit card number, personal telephone number, or driver license number of any person ... except for use by any government agency, including any court or law enforcement agency, in carrying out its functions, or any private person or entity acting on behalf thereof, or any private person or entity seeking to enforce payment of court-ordered child support
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(a), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: 2024 amendment changed 'unlisted telephone number' to 'personal telephone number.' A broader draft redaction (email/medical/financial/personal info) was NOT enacted (deleted in the second reprint).

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory redaction of covered-officer home address (Daniel's Law)
rules.atomic_rule: Prior to allowing access, the custodian shall redact, per P.L.2021, c.371, the home address (primary or secondary) of any active, formerly active, or retired judicial officer, prosecutor, law enforcement officer, or child protective investigator in DCP&P, or any immediate family member.
rules.trigger: Record to be disclosed contains the home address of a covered person or immediate family member
rules.source_language: the custodian thereof shall redact from that record any information which discloses ... in accordance with section 2 of P.L.2021, c.371 (C.47:1B-2), the home address, whether a primary or secondary residence, of any active, formerly active, or retired judicial officer, prosecutor, law enforcement officer, or child protective investigator in the Division of Child Protection and Permanency, or, as defined in section 1 of P.L.2021, c.371 (C.47:1B-1), any immediate family member thereof
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(a), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Redaction operationalized through the Office of Information Privacy approval process (NJ-T38); triggers the 14-day review window (NJ-T03).

rules.legal_concept: Segregate exempt portion and produce remainder
rules.atomic_rule: If the custodian asserts part of a record is exempt, the custodian shall delete or excise from a copy the portion asserted exempt and shall promptly permit access to the remainder of the record.
rules.trigger: Custodian asserts part of a particular record is exempt from access
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: 'promptly' permit access to remainder
rules.source_language: If the custodian of a government record asserts that part of a particular record is exempt from public access pursuant to P.L.1963, c.73 (C.47:1A-1 et seq.) as amended and supplemented, the custodian shall delete or excise from a copy of the record that portion which the custodian asserts is exempt from access and shall promptly permit access to the remainder of the record.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Core segregability duty; 'promptly' is a soft production standard for the non-exempt remainder.

rules.legal_concept: 30-day compliance to redact OIP-approved covered-person address
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency shall redact or cease disclosing the home address of a covered person approved by the Office of Information Privacy no later than 30 days following the approval, and shall discontinue redaction for an approved revocation within 30 days of that approval.
rules.trigger: Office of Information Privacy approves a covered-person redaction (or revocation) request
rules.clock_spec: 30 calendar-days from OIP approval
rules.source_language: A public agency shall redact or cease to disclose, in accordance with section 6 of P.L.2001, c.404 (C.47:1A-5) and section 1 of P.L.1995, c.23 (C.47:1A-1.1), respectively, the home address of a covered person approved by the Office of Information Privacy not later than 30 days following the approval. A public agency shall also discontinue the redaction or nondisclosure of the home address of any covered person for whom a revocation request has been approved not later than 30 days following the approval.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1B-2(b)(1), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.6
rules.notes: Redaction compliance window keyed to an external OIP approval event, not to a records request.

rules.legal_concept: Criminal-investigation information within 24 hours
rules.atomic_rule: Enumerated information concerning a criminal investigation shall be available to the public within 24 hours or as soon as practicable of a request for such information.
rules.trigger: Request for enumerated criminal-investigation information
rules.clock_spec: 24 hours (or 'as soon as practicable') from request
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding the provisions of P.L.1963, c. 73 (C. 47:1A-1 et seq.), as amended and supplemented, the following information concerning a criminal investigation shall be available to the public within 24 hours or as soon as practicable, of a request for such information:
rules.effective_status: Current (P.L. 2001, c.404, s.4; not amended by P.L. 2024, c.16)
rules.notes: Distinct expedited special-records workflow. Source: GRC official 'Readable Version' PDF (this section unchanged by the 2024 amendments). Hybrid 24-hour ceiling with an 'as soon as practicable' soft alternative.

rules.legal_concept: Office of the Public Defender case files confidential
rules.atomic_rule: Files maintained by the Office of the Public Defender that relate to the handling of any case are confidential and not open to inspection unless authorized by law, court order, or the State Public Defender.
rules.trigger: Request for Office of the Public Defender case-handling files
rules.source_language: The files maintained by the Office of the Public Defender that relate to the handling of any case shall be considered confidential and shall not be open to inspection by any person unless authorized by law, court order, or the State Public Defender.
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(k), as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.2
rules.notes: Special-record classification routing a request to a confidential-unless-authorized branch.

rules.legal_concept: Limited redaction of election records by election agencies
rules.atomic_rule: For enumerated election records, an election agency shall not redact the provided information except for voter signatures, Social Security numbers, driver license numbers, and non-driver identification numbers.
rules.trigger: Request to an election agency for enumerated election records
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding any other law, rule, or regulation to the contrary, except as otherwise provided in sections 2 and 3 of P.L.2021, c.371 (C.47:1B-1 et seq.), subsection b. of section 1 of P.L.1994, c.148 (C.19:31-3.2), or in any rules or regulations promulgated by the Secretary of State pursuant to subsection f. of this section, the following shall be records for which the provided information shall not be redacted by an election agency except for voter signatures, Social Security numbers, driver license numbers, and non-driver identification numbers:
rules.effective_status: Effective September 3, 2024 (P.L. 2024, c.16, new section); current
rules.notes: Special election-agency redaction rule narrowing redactable fields for voter-registration, party-affiliation, VBM applications, nominating/recall/public-question petitions, and related submissions.

rules.legal_concept: Two-business-day immediate access to election records
