rules.atomic_rule: An election agency shall make enumerated election records available for immediate access and email transmission as soon as possible but not later than two business days after receipt of the request, provided the request is not for a commercial purpose, with no fee charged.
rules.trigger: Non-commercial request to an election agency for enumerated election records (filed within preceding 90 days)
rules.clock_spec: 2 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding any other law, rule, or regulation to the contrary, the following shall be records and information that an election agency shall make available to requestors for immediate access and transmission via email as soon as possible, but not later than two business days after receipt of the request, provided the request is not for a commercial purpose, for which a fee shall not be charged nor collected:
rules.effective_status: Effective September 3, 2024 (P.L. 2024, c.16, new section); current
rules.notes: Special expedited election workflow; commercial requests fall outside this expedited/no-fee track.

rules.legal_concept: Election-eve expedited access to voter lists
rules.atomic_rule: For non-commercial requests pertaining only to an election within 16 days, election agencies shall provide enumerated voter lists for immediate access; transmission is not later than two business days after receipt when the request is made 1-15 days before the election, and a request submitted by noon the day before an election must be completed by noon on election day, with no fee.
rules.trigger: Non-commercial request pertaining only to an election within 16 days
rules.clock_spec: 2 business-days from receipt (1-15 days pre-election); if submitted by noon day-before-election, complete by noon election day
rules.source_language: the following in paragraphs (1) through (4) of this subsection shall be records and information that an election agency shall make available to requestors for immediate access and transmission via email as soon as possible, provided the request pertains only to an election to be held within 16 days after the date of the request and is not for a commercial purpose. The transmission shall be not later than two business days after receipt of the request when said request is made between one and 15 days before the date of the election pertaining to the request. For any request submitted the day before an election by noon, the request shall be completed by noon the day of the election. A fee shall not be charged nor collected.
rules.effective_status: Effective September 3, 2024 (P.L. 2024, c.16, new section); current
rules.notes: Bespoke election-eve deadline fork (noon-before/noon-of); privacy-preserving production required where disclosure would violate a voter's privacy.

rules.legal_concept: Website posting satisfies election-record deadlines
rules.atomic_rule: The inspection and transmission deadline requirements are deemed satisfied if the election agency posts the records and information on its website.
rules.trigger: Election agency posts the applicable election records on its website
rules.clock_spec: deadline requirement deemed satisfied upon website posting
rules.source_language: The inspection and transmission deadline requirements of this subsection shall be deemed satisfied if an election agency posts on its website the records and information referred to in this subsection.
rules.effective_status: Effective September 3, 2024 (P.L. 2024, c.16, new section); current
rules.notes: Satisfies both the two-business-day (c) and election-eve (d) deadlines.

rules.legal_concept: Court protective order for requests intended to interrupt government function
rules.atomic_rule: On a verified complaint proven by clear and convincing evidence that a requestor sought records with intent to substantially interrupt the performance of government function, the court may issue a protective order limiting the number and scope of requests or waiving the required response time, and may limit or eliminate the agency's duty to respond to that requestor's future requests.
rules.trigger: Court finds, by clear and convincing evidence, intent to substantially interrupt government function
rules.clock_spec: court may waive the required response time; may limit or eliminate future response duty (terminal for future requests)
rules.source_language: the court may issue a protective order limiting the number and scope of requests the requestor may make or order such other relief as it deems appropriate, including referral of the matter to mediation or a waiver of the required response time. ... The order specified in subsection a. of this section may limit, or, in appropriate circumstances, eliminate the public agency's duty to respond to government records requests from the requestor in the future.
rules.effective_status: Effective September 3, 2024 (P.L. 2024, c.16, new section); current
rules.notes: Court-issued path that tolls/eliminates the response clock. Labor-organization/collective-bargaining requests are statutorily excluded from being the basis of such a complaint.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'commercial purpose'
rules.atomic_rule: 'Commercial purpose' means direct or indirect use of any part of a government record for sale, resale, solicitation, rent, or lease of a service, or any use by which the user expects a profit; it excludes use by the news media, news/journalistic/educational/scientific/scholarly/governmental organizations, authorized campaign/committee agents, labor organizations, and CBA-signatory contractors seeking enforcement information.
rules.trigger: Requestor certifies (or request is identified as) commercial-purpose use
rules.source_language: "Commercial purpose" means the direct or indirect use of any part of a government record for sale, resale, solicitation, rent, or lease of a service, or any use by which the user expects a profit either through commission, salary, or fee. "Commercial purpose" shall not include the use of a government record for any purpose by: (1) the news media, or any parent company, subsidiary, or affiliate of any news media, as defined by section 2 of P.L.1977, c.253 (C.2A:84A-21a); (2) any news, journalistic, educational, scientific, scholarly, or governmental organization; (3) any person authorized to act on behalf of a candidate committee, joint candidate committee, political committee, continuing political committee, political party committee, or legislative leadership committee ...; (4) any labor organization; (5) any contractor signatory to a collective bargaining agreement seeking information material to the enforcement of State or federal statutes or regulations regarding, but not limited to, wage and hour protections ...
rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-1.1, as amended by P.L. 2024, c.16, s.1
rules.notes: Definition the engine branches on: commercial purpose drives the 14-business-day window (NJ-T02), the expedite-fee option (NJ-T06), and fee treatment (Fees sibling).

rules.legal_concept: Statutory per-page duplication fee for printed matter
rules.atomic_rule: For a government record embodied in printed matter, the custodian shall assess a duplication fee of $0.05 per letter-size page or smaller and $0.07 per legal-size page or larger.
rules.trigger: Requestor purchases a copy of a printed government record
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law or regulation and except as provided in paragraph (2) of this subsection, the fee assessed for the duplication of a government record embodied in the form of printed matter shall be $0.05 per letter size page or smaller, and $0.07 per legal size page or larger.
rules.notes: Set as a fixed statutory amount, not a ceiling; 'except as otherwise provided by law or regulation' allows a different rate where another statute/regulation prescribes one.

rules.atomic_rule: Access to electronic records and non-printed materials shall be provided free of charge (fee = $0).
rules.trigger: Record requested in electronic or non-printed form
rules.source_language: Access to electronic records and non-printed materials shall be provided free of charge, but the public agency may charge for the actual costs of any needed supplies such as computer discs.
rules.notes: Split from the supply-cost permission (NJ-M03), which is bundled in the same sentence.

rules.atomic_rule: When providing electronic/non-printed records free of charge, the public agency may charge for the actual costs of any needed supplies such as computer discs.
rules.trigger: Supplies (e.g., discs) needed to deliver electronic records
rules.source_language: Access to electronic records and non-printed materials shall be provided free of charge, but the public agency may charge for the actual costs of any needed supplies such as computer discs.
rules.notes: 'Actual costs' is an undefined-cost standard, not a fixed rate.

rules.atomic_rule: No fee shall be charged if the request is completed by directing the requestor to the record available on the public agency's website or another public agency's website.
rules.trigger: Requested record is available on a public agency website and request is completed by direction to it
rules.source_language: No fee shall be charged if the request is completed by directing the requestor to the requested government record that is available on the public agency's website or the website of another public agency.
rules.notes: If requestor still cannot find the record and requests a physical copy, a capped fee applies (NJ-M11).

rules.atomic_rule: No fee shall be charged to a victim of a crime for a copy of a record to which the crime victim is entitled to access.
rules.trigger: Requestor is a crime victim entitled to the record under C.47:1A-1.1
rules.source_language: No fee shall be charged to a victim of a crime for a copy or copies of a record to which the crime victim is entitled to access, as provided in section 1 of P.L.1995, c.23 (C.47:1A-1.1).

rules.legal_concept: Special service charge for extraordinary printed-record requests
rules.atomic_rule: Where a printed record cannot be reproduced by ordinary copying equipment or involves an extraordinary expenditure of time and effort, the agency may charge, in addition to actual duplication cost, a reasonable special service charge based on the actual direct cost of providing the copies.
rules.trigger: Nature, format, collation or volume of a printed record makes it unreproducible by ordinary equipment or requires extraordinary time/effort
rules.source_language: Whenever the nature, format, manner of collation, or volume of a government record embodied in the form of printed matter to be inspected, examined, or copied pursuant to this section is such that the record cannot be reproduced by ordinary document copying equipment in ordinary business size or involves an extraordinary expenditure of time and effort to accommodate the request, the public agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplicating the record, a special service charge that shall be based upon the actual direct cost of providing the copy or copies, and such special service charge shall be reasonable.
rules.notes: Amount is bounded by a 'reasonable / actual direct cost' standard, not a number.

rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall provide the requestor with an explanation for, and an itemized list of, the fees or charges.
rules.trigger: Fees or charges (including special service charges) are to be assessed
rules.source_language: The custodian shall provide the requestor with an explanation for and an itemized list of the fees or charges.
rules.notes: Required document/notice generated during request handling.

rules.atomic_rule: The requestor shall have the opportunity to review and object to any fee or charge before it is incurred.
rules.trigger: A fee or charge is proposed
rules.source_language: The requestor shall have the opportunity to review and object to any fee or charge prior to it being incurred.
rules.notes: A required state/step: pre-charge review-and-object gate before charges are incurred.

rules.atomic_rule: Fees/charges presented by the custodian are rebuttably presumed reasonable; if the requestor objects, the requestor bears the burden of proving the fees or charges are unreasonable.
rules.trigger: Requestor objects to a fee or charge
rules.source_language: There shall be a rebuttable presumption that the fees or charges presented by the custodian are reasonable. If the requestor objects to the fees or charges, the burden of proof shall be on the requestor to demonstrate that the fees or charges are unreasonable.
rules.notes: Burden-allocation rule; 2024 amendment placed the burden on the requestor.

rules.atomic_rule: If the agency converts a record to a requested medium/format, it may charge, in addition to actual duplication cost, a reasonable special service fee based on the cost of extensive IT use or the labor cost of personnel providing the service.
rules.trigger: Agency converts a record to a medium/format it does not maintain
rules.source_language: If the public agency converts the record to the medium or format requested, the agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplication, a special service fee that shall be reasonable and shall be based on the cost for any extensive use of information technology, or for the labor cost of personnel providing the service, that is actually incurred by the agency or attributable to the agency for the programming, clerical, and supervisory assistance required, or both.

rules.atomic_rule: Where a requestor directed to a website record still cannot find it and requests a physical copy, the custodian shall provide a physical copy for a fee not exceeding two times the cost of production of the document.
rules.trigger: Requestor directed to website record cannot locate it after custodian assistance and requests a physical copy
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 2x cost of production
rules.source_language: If the requestor is still unable to locate the record and requests a physical copy, the custodian shall provide the requestor with a physical copy of the record for a fee not exceeding two times the cost of the production of the document.
rules.notes: Clock Spec cell used here to carry the fee ceiling (2x), not a time value.

rules.atomic_rule: If a commercial requestor wants the record within seven business days (rather than the 14-day commercial window), the custodian may charge a special service fee not exceeding two times the cost of production of the record.
rules.trigger: Commercial-purpose requestor elects expedited (7 business-day) delivery
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 2x cost of production
rules.source_language: If a commercial requestor would like to receive the record within seven business days, as established in this subsection, the custodian shall provide the requestor with a copy of the record and may charge a special service fee not exceeding two times the cost of the production of the record.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'commercial purpose' governing fee basis and response time
rules.atomic_rule: A request has a 'commercial purpose' where any part of the record is used, directly or indirectly, for sale, resale, solicitation, rent, or lease of a service, or any use by which the user expects a profit through commission, salary, or fee; this classification triggers the 14-business-day response window and special expedite fees.
rules.trigger: Requestor's certified use of the record
rules.source_language: "Commercial purpose" means the direct or indirect use of any part of a government record for sale, resale, solicitation, rent, or lease of a service or any use by which the user expects a profit either through commission, salary, or fee.
rules.notes: Definition the software branches on (fee basis + response-time fork). Excludes use by news media (and other listed exclusions not reproduced here). Requestor must certify commercial purpose for the request to be fulfilled; intentional failure to certify carries a penalty (NJ-M55).

rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may require prepayment of fees or a deposit, and the request form must state whether prepayment of fees or a deposit is required.
rules.trigger: Fees or a deposit are required to process the request
rules.source_language: The form shall also include the following: ... (2) a statement as to whether prepayment of fees or a deposit is required; ... The custodian may require a deposit against costs for reproducing documents sought through a request whenever the custodian anticipates that the information thus requested will cost in excess of $5 to reproduce.
rules.notes: Split from the $5 deposit threshold (NJ-M15).

rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may require a deposit against costs whenever the custodian anticipates the requested reproduction will cost in excess of $5.
rules.trigger: Custodian anticipates reproduction cost exceeding $5
rules.source_language: The custodian may require a deposit against costs for reproducing documents sought through a request whenever the custodian anticipates that the information thus requested will cost in excess of $5 to reproduce.
rules.notes: $5 is a fixed statutory trigger threshold for the deposit permission.

rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may deny a request that is incomplete (missing information required on the adopted form), including a letter/email request that omits all required information.
rules.trigger: Request omits information required on the adopted request form
rules.source_language: A request shall be submitted by a requestor in the form adopted by the custodian and the custodian may deny a request that is incomplete, except that a requestor indicating the request is being submitted anonymously shall not be grounds for denial. ... If a letter or an email from a requestor does not include all of the information required on the adopted form, the custodian may deny the record request.

rules.atomic_rule: A request submitted anonymously shall not be considered incomplete and anonymity is not grounds for denial.
rules.trigger: Requestor indicates the request is submitted anonymously
rules.source_language: A request may be submitted anonymously provided, however, that anonymous requestors shall not be permitted to institute proceedings pursuant to section 7 of P.L.2001, c.404 (C.47:1A-6). A request that is submitted anonymously shall not be considered incomplete.
rules.notes: Anonymity permitted for the request but bars later appeal/proceedings (see NJ-M31).

rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may deny a letter/email request that includes substantially more information than required on the form and requires more than reasonable effort to clarify.
rules.trigger: Letter/email request contains substantially excess information requiring more than reasonable clarification effort
rules.source_language: If the letter or email from a requestor includes substantially more information than required on the adopted form and requires more than reasonable effort to clarify the information, the custodian may deny the request.

rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may deny repeated requests submitted to multiple custodians in the same public agency for the same record while an identical or substantially similar request is pending in that agency.
rules.trigger: Repeated submissions to multiple custodians in one agency for the same record while a like request is pending
rules.source_language: Submission of repeated requests to multiple custodians in the same public agency for the same record, while an identical or substantially similar request is pending in the agency, shall permit the custodian to deny the request.

rules.atomic_rule: If unable to comply with a request, the custodian shall indicate the specific basis on the request form, promptly return it to the requestor, and sign, date, and provide the requestor a copy.
rules.trigger: Custodian is unable to comply with (denies) a request for access
rules.source_language: If the custodian is unable to comply with a request for access, the custodian shall indicate the specific basis therefor on the request form and promptly return it to the requestor. The custodian shall sign and date the form and provide the requestor with a copy thereof.
rules.notes: Required written-denial notice with specific basis; 'promptly' is an undefined-soft timing standard on the return.

rules.atomic_rule: If a request would substantially disrupt agency operations, the custodian may deny access after informing the requestor of the potential disruption and attempting to reach a reasonable solution accommodating both parties' interests.
rules.trigger: Request would substantially disrupt agency operations
rules.source_language: If a request for access to a government record would substantially disrupt agency operations, the custodian may deny access to the record after informing the requestor of the potential disruption to agency operations and attempting to reach a reasonable solution with the requestor that accommodates the interests of the requestor and the agency.
rules.notes: Denial conditioned on a mandatory notice-and-negotiation step.

rules.atomic_rule: A party to a legal proceeding may not request a record that is the subject of a court order (including a pending discovery request); the custodian shall not be required to complete such a request, and the requestor must certify whether the record is sought in connection with a legal proceeding.
rules.trigger: Requestor is a party to a legal proceeding and the record is subject to a court order or pending discovery request
rules.source_language: A party to a legal proceeding may not request a government record if the record sought is the subject of a court order, including a pending discovery request, and a custodian shall not be required to complete such a request. The requestor shall be required to certify whether the government record is being sought in connection with a legal proceeding and identify the proceeding for the request to be fulfilled.
rules.notes: Carve-out: does not bar requests by a labor organization or CBA-signatory contractor for enforcement-related information not sought in furtherance of litigation discovery (see NJ-M61).

rules.atomic_rule: The custodian is not required to complete a request (e.g., for mail, email, texts, correspondence, social media) that does not identify a specific job title/accounts, a specific subject matter, and a reasonable time period, or that would require research and creation of new records.
rules.trigger: Request lacks specific job title/accounts, subject matter, or reasonable time period, or would require research/creation of new records
rules.source_language: A custodian shall not be required to complete a request, including for, but not limited to, mail, email, text messages, correspondence, or social media postings and messages, if the request does not identify a specific job title or accounts to be searched, a specific subject matter, and is not confined to a reasonable time period, or if the custodian determines that the request would require research and the collection of information from the contents of government records and the creation of new government records setting forth that research and information.

rules.atomic_rule: The custodian is not required to complete an identical request from the same requestor if the information has not changed (periodic requests for regularly-updated records remain permitted).
rules.trigger: Same requestor submits an identical request and the information has not changed
rules.source_language: The custodian shall not be required to complete an identical request for access to a government record from the same requestor if the information has not changed. Nothing in this section shall prevent a requestor from filing periodic requests regarding regularly updated public records, including, but not limited to, certified payrolls, permits, and licensing applications.

rules.legal_concept: Constructive (deemed) denial on custodian's failure to respond
rules.atomic_rule: If the custodian fails to respond within seven business days (or 14 business days for commercial-purpose/redaction-review requests) after receiving a request, the failure to respond is deemed a denial of the request.
rules.trigger: Custodian does not respond within the applicable 7- or 14-business-day period
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from request receipt (14 business-days if commercial purpose or C.47:1B compliance review); +7 business-days for a fire district with one or fewer full-time custodial employees
rules.source_language: In the event a custodian fails to respond within seven business days or 14 business days, as appropriate, after receiving a request, the failure to respond shall be deemed a denial of the request, unless the requestor has elected not to accurately identify themselves or to provide an accurate address, email address, or telephone number.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: constructive-denial trigger (clock with terminal event). The underlying 7/14-day response deadline itself is a Deadlines-category rule (sibling scope). During a declared state of emergency the deadlines do not apply.

rules.atomic_rule: Where the requestor elected not to accurately identify themselves or provide an accurate address/email/phone, the deemed-denial does not run and the custodian need not respond until the requestor contacts the custodian seeking a response.
rules.trigger: Requestor did not accurately identify themselves or provide accurate contact information
rules.clock_spec: response obligation suspended until requestor contacts custodian seeking a response
rules.source_language: If the requestor has elected not to accurately identify themselves or to provide an accurate address, email address, or telephone number, the custodian shall not be required to respond until the requestor contacts the custodian seeking a response to the original request.

rules.atomic_rule: If the record is in storage or archived, the requestor must be so advised within 7/14 business days and told when the record can be made available, which shall be no more than 21 business days from that advisory; if not made available by then, access is deemed denied.
rules.trigger: Requested record is in storage or archived
rules.clock_spec: advise within 7/14 business-days of receipt; availability no more than 21 business-days from the advisory; non-availability = deemed denied
rules.source_language: If the government record is in storage or archived, the requestor shall be so advised within seven or 14 business days, as appropriate, after the custodian receives the request. The requestor shall be advised by the custodian when the record can be made available, which shall be no more than 21 business days from the date the requestor is so advised. If the record is not made available by that time, access shall be deemed denied.
rules.notes: Storage/archived processing branch with its own terminal deemed-denial.

rules.legal_concept: Judicial challenge to denial in Superior Court
rules.atomic_rule: A requestor accurately identified by name who is denied access may, within 45 days of the date of denial, institute a proceeding in Superior Court challenging the custodian's decision, heard by a designated Superior Court judge.
rules.trigger: Requestor is denied access to a government record
rules.clock_spec: 45 calendar-days from date of denial
rules.source_language: A person who is denied access to a government record by the custodian of the record, at the option of the requestor who is accurately identified by name, may, within 45 days of the date of denial: institute a proceeding to challenge the custodian's decision by filing an action in Superior Court which shall be heard in the vicinage where it is filed by a Superior Court Judge who has been designated to hear such cases because of that judge's knowledge and expertise in matters relating to access to government records;
rules.notes: 2024 amendment added the 45-day limitations period and the named-requestor requirement (previously no fixed deadline).

rules.legal_concept: Administrative complaint to the Government Records Council
rules.atomic_rule: In lieu of a Superior Court action, a denied requestor may, within 45 days of the date of denial, file a complaint with the Government Records Council.
rules.trigger: Requestor is denied access and elects the administrative forum
rules.clock_spec: 45 calendar-days from date of denial
rules.source_language: in lieu of filing an action in Superior Court, file a complaint with the Government Records Council established pursuant to section 8 of P.L.2001, c.404 (C.47:1A-7).
rules.notes: Structural forum election: Superior Court OR GRC (mutually exclusive 'in lieu of'). Both share the 45-day window.

rules.atomic_rule: The right to institute a proceeding challenging a denial is solely that of the requestor, who must be accurately identified by name.
rules.trigger: Initiation of a denial-challenge proceeding
rules.source_language: The right to institute any proceeding under this section shall be solely that of the requestor.

rules.atomic_rule: An anonymous requestor is not permitted to institute proceedings under N.J.S.A. 47:1A-6.
rules.trigger: Request was submitted anonymously
rules.source_language: anonymous requestors shall not be permitted to institute proceedings pursuant to section 7 of P.L.2001, c.404 (C.47:1A-6).

rules.atomic_rule: Any proceeding challenging a denial shall proceed in a summary or expedited manner.
rules.trigger: A denial-challenge proceeding is instituted (Superior Court or GRC)
rules.source_language: Any such proceeding shall proceed in a summary or expedited manner.

rules.atomic_rule: In a denial-challenge proceeding, the public agency has the burden of proving that the denial of access is authorized by law.
rules.trigger: Denial is challenged before a court or the GRC
rules.source_language: The public agency shall have the burden of proving that the denial of access is authorized by law.

rules.atomic_rule: If it is determined that access was improperly denied, the court or the Government Records Council shall order that access be allowed.
rules.trigger: Adjudicator finds access was improperly denied
rules.source_language: If it is determined that access has been improperly denied, the court or Government Records Council shall order that access be allowed.

rules.atomic_rule: A decision of the Government Records Council may be appealed to the Appellate Division of the Superior Court, filed within 45 days from the date the council renders its decision.
rules.trigger: GRC renders a decision a party wishes to appeal
rules.clock_spec: 45 calendar-days from date GRC renders decision
rules.source_language: A decision of the council may be appealed to the Appellate Division of the Superior Court. Such appeals shall be filed within 45 days from the date the council renders a decision.

rules.atomic_rule: A decision of the Government Records Council has no value as precedent for any case initiated in Superior Court under N.J.S.A. 47:1A-6.
rules.trigger: GRC has rendered a decision; a separate Superior Court case exists
rules.source_language: A decision of the council shall not have value as a precedent for any case initiated in Superior Court pursuant to section 7 of P.L.2001, c.404 (C.47:1A-6).

rules.legal_concept: GRC authority to receive, hear, review, and adjudicate denial complaints
rules.atomic_rule: The Government Records Council shall receive, hear, review, and adjudicate a complaint filed by any person concerning a denial of access to a government record by a records custodian.
rules.trigger: A person files a complaint alleging denial of access
rules.source_language: receive, hear, review and adjudicate a complaint filed by any person concerning a denial of access to a government record by a records custodian;

rules.atomic_rule: The Government Records Council shall establish an informal mediation program to facilitate resolution of disputes regarding access to government records.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing obligation of the council)
rules.source_language: establish an informal mediation program to facilitate the resolution of disputes regarding access to government records;

rules.atomic_rule: Upon receipt of a written complaint alleging improper denial, the council shall offer the parties the opportunity to resolve the dispute through mediation by a neutral mediator selected by the council.
rules.trigger: Council receives a written, signed complaint alleging improper denial
rules.source_language: Upon receipt of a written complaint signed by any person alleging that a custodian of a government record has improperly denied that person access to a government record, the council shall offer the parties the opportunity to resolve the dispute through mediation.

rules.atomic_rule: If any party declines mediation or mediation fails to resolve the matter to all parties' satisfaction, the council shall initiate an investigation of the facts and circumstances in the complaint.
rules.trigger: A party declines mediation or mediation fails
rules.source_language: If any party declines mediation or if mediation fails to resolve the matter to the satisfaction of all parties, the council shall initiate an investigation concerning the facts and circumstances set forth in the complaint.

rules.atomic_rule: The council shall determine whether the complaint is within its jurisdiction or is frivolous or without any reasonable factual basis; if outside jurisdiction, frivolous, or without factual basis, it shall reduce that conclusion to writing and transmit copies to the complainant and the agency.
rules.trigger: Council initiates investigation after mediation is declined or fails
rules.source_language: The council shall make a determination as to whether the complaint is within its jurisdiction or frivolous or without any reasonable factual basis. ... If the council shall conclude that the complaint is outside its jurisdiction, frivolous, or without factual basis, it shall reduce that conclusion to writing and transmit a copy thereof to the complainant and to the public agency that employs the records custodian against whom the complaint was filed.

rules.atomic_rule: The public agency employing the custodian shall have the opportunity to present the council with any statement or information concerning the complaint.
rules.trigger: Council notifies the agency of the complaint
rules.source_language: The public agency that employs the records custodian shall have the opportunity to present the board with any statement or information concerning the complaint which the agency wishes.

rules.atomic_rule: If the council cannot determine a record's accessibility from the complaint and the agency's response, it shall conduct a hearing in conformity with the rules for State-agency contested cases under the Administrative Procedure Act.
rules.trigger: Council is unable to determine accessibility on the papers
rules.source_language: If the council is unable to make a determination as to a record's accessibility based upon the complaint and the agency's response thereto, the council shall conduct a hearing on the matter in conformity with the rules and regulations provided for hearings by a State agency in contested cases under the "Administrative Procedure Act," P.L.1968, c.410 (C.52:14B-1 et seq.), insofar as they may be applicable and practicable.

rules.atomic_rule: The council shall, by majority vote of its members, render a decision as to whether the record at issue must be made available for public access.
rules.trigger: Council concludes its review/hearing
rules.source_language: The council shall, by a majority vote of its members, render a decision as to whether the record which is the subject of the complaint is a government record which must be made available for public access pursuant to P.L.1963, c.73 (C.47:1A-1 et seq.) as amended and supplemented.

rules.atomic_rule: The Government Records Council shall not charge any party a fee in regard to actions filed with the council.
rules.trigger: A party files an action with the council
rules.source_language: The council shall not charge any party a fee in regard to actions filed with the council.

rules.atomic_rule: The council has no jurisdiction over the Judicial or Legislative Branches of State Government or any agency, officer, or employee of those branches.
rules.trigger: Complaint targets a Judicial- or Legislative-branch entity
rules.source_language: The council shall not have jurisdiction over the Judicial or Legislative Branches of State Government or any agency, officer, or employee of those branches.

rules.legal_concept: 90-day GRC adjudication deadline
rules.atomic_rule: Beginning 18 months after the effective date of P.L.2024, c.16, the council shall adjudicate all complaints within 90 days of filing, extendable 45 days for good cause, exclusive of time during which parties are engaged in mediation.
rules.trigger: A complaint comes before the council (on or after ~March 3, 2026)
rules.clock_spec: 90 calendar-days from complaint filing (+45-day good-cause extension), excluding mediation periods
rules.source_language: Beginning 18 months following the effective date of P.L.2024, c.16 (C.47:1A-5.1 et al.), the council shall adjudicate all complaints that come before it within 90 days of the complaint's filing, with the ability to extend for 45 days for good cause, exclusive of any time period during which the parties are engaged in a mediation process pursuant to this section.
rules.effective_status: Current — in effect on/after ~March 3, 2026 (18 months after Sept. 3, 2024 effective date)
rules.notes: Delayed-onset deadline; the 18-month ramp has elapsed as of the research date (2026-07-21), so it now governs.

rules.atomic_rule: At the council's request, a public agency shall produce documents and ensure the attendance of witnesses for the council's investigation of any complaint or the holding of any hearing.
rules.trigger: Council requests documents/witnesses for an investigation or hearing
rules.source_language: At the request of the council, a public agency shall produce documents and ensure the attendance of witnesses with respect to the council's investigation of any complaint or the holding of any hearing.

rules.atomic_rule: The council may go into closed session during the portion of any proceeding in which the contents of a contested record would be disclosed.
rules.trigger: A proceeding would disclose the contents of a contested record
rules.source_language: The council shall be subject to the provisions of the "Open Public Meetings Act," P.L.1975, c.231 (C.10:4-6), except that the council may go into closed session during that portion of any proceeding during which the contents of a contested record would be disclosed.

rules.atomic_rule: Complaints/appeals pending before the GRC or Superior Court that were filed anonymously or under a fictitious identity before the Act's effective date may be dismissed with prejudice on the agency's motion unless the complainant amends to accurately identify name and mailing address within 90 days of the effective date.
rules.trigger: Pre-effective-date pending complaint/appeal filed anonymously or under a fictitious identity
rules.clock_spec: amendment within 90 calendar-days of the Sept. 3, 2024 effective date (window closed ~Dec. 2, 2024)
rules.source_language: All complaints and appeals pending before the Government Records Council or the Superior Court filed prior to the effective date of P.L.2024, c.16 (C.47:1A-5.1 et al.), either anonymously or using a fictitious name or identity, may be dismissed with prejudice upon a motion by the public agency, unless the complainant files an amendment to their complaint that accurately identifies their name and mailing address within 90 days of the effective date of P.L.2024, c.16 (C.47:1A-5.1 et al.).
rules.effective_status: Transitional — 90-day amendment window expired ~Dec. 2, 2024; provision now spent for new matters
rules.notes: One-time transitional rule; retained for completeness. No longer alters handling of new requests.

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary attorney-fee award to prevailing requestor
rules.atomic_rule: A requestor who prevails in any proceeding may be entitled to a reasonable attorney's fee (discretionary).
rules.trigger: Requestor prevails in a Superior Court or GRC proceeding
rules.source_language: A requestor who prevails in any proceeding may be entitled to a reasonable attorney's fee. While the court or Government Records Council may award a reasonable attorney's fee to a prevailing party in any proceeding,
rules.notes: Major 2024 change: prior law mandated ('shall') fee-shifting to all prevailing requestors; now discretionary ('may') unless the aggravating findings in NJ-M52 apply.

rules.atomic_rule: If the agency is determined to have unreasonably denied access, acted in bad faith, or knowingly and willfully violated OPRA, the court or GRC shall award a reasonable attorney's fee.
rules.trigger: Determination that the agency unreasonably denied access, acted in bad faith, or knowingly and willfully violated OPRA
rules.source_language: if the public agency has been determined to have unreasonably denied access, acted in bad faith, or knowingly and willfully violated P.L.1963, c.73 (C.47:1A-1 et seq.), then the court or Government Records Council shall award a reasonable attorney's fee.

rules.atomic_rule: If the agency produces the records within seven business days of service of a Superior Court action or GRC complaint, upon notification the matter shall be dismissed without prejudice; the requestor may still be entitled to a reasonable attorney's fee if the custodian knew or should have known the denial violated OPRA.
rules.trigger: Agency produces the records within 7 business days of service of the action/complaint
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from service of the Superior Court action or GRC complaint
rules.source_language: If the records sought are produced by the public agency within seven business days of service of an action in Superior Court or a complaint before the Government Records Council, upon notification to the Superior Court or the Government Records Council, the matter shall be dismissed without prejudice and the requestor may be entitled to a reasonable attorney's fee if the custodian knew or should have known that the denial of access violated P.L.1963, c.73 (C.47:1A-1 et seq.).

rules.legal_concept: Escalating civil penalties for knowing and willful OPRA violations
rules.atomic_rule: Where a public official/officer/employee/custodian is found to have knowingly and willfully violated OPRA and to have unreasonably denied access under the totality of the circumstances, the employing agency is subject to a civil penalty of $1,000 (initial), $2,500 (second within 10 years), and $5,000 (third within 10 years); penalties may be imposed by the courts or the GRC.
rules.trigger: Finding of a knowing and willful violation plus unreasonable denial under the totality of the circumstances
rules.clock_spec: amounts: $1,000 initial / $2,500 second (within 10 yrs) / $5,000 third (within 10 yrs)
rules.source_language: If a public official, officer, employee, or custodian is found to have knowingly and willfully violated P.L.1963, c.73 (C.47:1A-1 et seq.), as amended and supplemented, and to have unreasonably denied access under the totality of the circumstances, the public agency that employs the custodian, officer, employee, or official shall be subject to a civil penalty of $1,000 for an initial violation, $2,500 for a second violation that occurs within 10 years of an initial violation, and $5,000 for a third violation that occurs within 10 years of an initial violation. The penalties authorized pursuant to this subsection may be imposed by the courts or by the Government Records Council.
rules.notes: 2024 amendment shifted liability to the employing agency (previously the individual custodian) and added the 'unreasonably denied under totality' element and the 10-year recidivism windows.

rules.atomic_rule: A requestor found to have intentionally failed to certify that a records request is for a commercial purpose is subject to a civil penalty of $1,000 (first offense), $2,500 (second), and $5,000 (each subsequent offense), imposable by the courts.
rules.trigger: Requestor intentionally fails to certify a commercial-purpose request
rules.clock_spec: amounts: $1,000 first / $2,500 second / $5,000 each subsequent
rules.source_language: A requestor who is found to have intentionally failed to certify that a records request is for a commercial purpose shall be subject to a civil penalty of $1,000 for the first offense, $2,500 for the second offense, and $5,000 for each subsequent offense. The penalties may be imposed by the courts.

rules.atomic_rule: Penalties are collected and enforced under the Penalty Enforcement Law of 1999 and the rules of court governing civil-penalty collection actions; the Superior Court has jurisdiction over collection and enforcement.
rules.trigger: A civil penalty has been imposed and requires collection
rules.source_language: These penalties shall be collected and enforced in proceedings in accordance with the "Penalty Enforcement Law of 1999," P.L.1999, c.274 (C.2A:58-10 et seq.), and the rules of court governing actions for the collection of civil penalties. The Superior Court shall have jurisdiction of proceedings for the collection and enforcement of the penalty imposed by this section.

rules.atomic_rule: Appropriate disciplinary proceedings may be initiated against a public official, officer, employee, or custodian against whom a penalty has been imposed.
rules.trigger: A penalty has been imposed on an official/officer/employee/custodian
rules.source_language: Appropriate disciplinary proceedings may be initiated against a public official, officer, employee or custodian against whom a penalty has been imposed.

rules.legal_concept: Protective order against requestor intending to interrupt government function
rules.atomic_rule: On a public agency's verified complaint, the Superior Court may issue a protective order limiting the number and scope of a requestor's requests (or other relief, including mediation referral or waiver of response time) if it finds by clear and convincing evidence that the requestor sought records with the intent to substantially interrupt the performance of government function; the complaint must include a declaration of compliance and good-faith effort at informal resolution, and proceeds summarily.
rules.trigger: Agency files a verified complaint alleging a requestor sought records with intent to substantially interrupt government function
rules.source_language: whenever there is filed a verified complaint to the Superior Court of the county in which the request for access to government records was made under P.L.1963, c.73 (C.47:1A-1 et seq.) alleging that a requestor has sought records with the intent to substantially interrupt the performance of government function, the court may issue a protective order limiting the number and scope of requests the requestor may make or order such other relief as it deems appropriate, including referral of the matter to mediation or a waiver of the required response time. The court may issue the protective order if it finds by clear and convincing evidence that the requestor has sought records under P.L.1963, c.73 (C.47:1A-1 et seq.) with the intent to substantially interrupt the performance of government function.
rules.notes: New in 2024. Requestor gets notice and opportunity to answer.

rules.atomic_rule: A protective order under 47:1A-5.1 may limit, or in appropriate circumstances eliminate, the public agency's duty to respond to future government-records requests from the requestor.
rules.trigger: Court issues a protective order under 47:1A-5.1
rules.source_language: The order specified in subsection a. of this section may limit, or, in appropriate circumstances, eliminate the public agency's duty to respond to government records requests from the requestor in the future.

rules.atomic_rule: In a protective-order proceeding under 47:1A-5.1, the public agency bears the burden of proof by clear and convincing evidence.
rules.trigger: Protective-order proceeding under 47:1A-5.1
rules.source_language: The public agency shall have the burden of proof by clear and convincing evidence.

rules.atomic_rule: Requests by a labor organization or CBA-signatory contractor seeking information material to enforcing State/federal wage-hour, workplace-safety, or public-procurement/bidding statutes (not sought in furtherance of litigation discovery) shall not be considered intended to interrupt government functions and cannot form the basis of a protective-order complaint.
rules.trigger: Request is filed by a qualifying labor organization or CBA-signatory contractor for enforcement-related information not tied to litigation discovery
rules.source_language: Requests for government records filed by a labor organization or by a contractor signatory to a collective bargaining agreement seeking information material to the enforcement of State or federal statutes or regulations regarding, but not limited to, wage and hour protections, workplace safety, or public procurement and public bidding, including, but not limited to, requests for certified payrolls or information about all bids submitted in response to a public procurement process subsequent to the deadline for the submission of all bids for that solicitation, when the request by the labor organization or contractor signatory is not sought in connection to or in furtherance of discovery requests in a court proceeding, shall not be considered to be intended to interrupt government functions, and shall not form the basis for the filing of a complaint under this section.

material_negatives.note: OPRA contains no mandatory clarification/deficiency-cure step or nonresponse-abandonment clock. When a request is incomplete, over-broad, or requires more than reasonable effort to clarify, the statute PERMITS denial (N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f), NJ-A14/NJ-A15) rather than requiring the custodian to seek clarification and toll a clock. The only affirmative negotiation duty is the 'reasonable solution' attempt for requests that would substantially disrupt operations (NJ-A24). No abandonment deadline for an unclarified request was found.

OPRA has no separate acknowledgment-of-receipt step distinct from the substantive grant/deny response deadline. There is no statutory duty to send an interim acknowledgment; the first required communication is the grant/deny (or storage/archive advisory) within the response window (Deadlines sibling).

No requestor identity-verification or proof-of-identity requirement at intake. Requests may be anonymous (NJ-A04); the only consequence of not accurately identifying is loss of standing to sue and suspension of the response duty until the requestor makes contact (NJ-A05). No government-ID or notarization requirement found.

No fixed numeric search-burden threshold (e.g., a maximum number of search hours or a defined 'unduly burdensome' cap) exists. Burden limits are expressed as soft standards - 'substantially disrupt agency operations' (NJ-A24) and 'reasonable time period' for correspondence (NJ-A26) - with no day/hour count.

The confidentiality/exemption catalogue within N.J.S.A. 47:1A-1.1 (deliberative/ACD material, criminal investigatory records, victims' records, legislative constituent records, etc.), the enacted 'personal identifying information' redaction definition, and the judicial-officer home-address protection (N.J.S.A. 47:1B-1/-2) are Denials/Redaction scope and are deferred to the sibling agent; only the core government-record and public-agency coverage definitions are captured here.

OPRA has no separate receipt-acknowledgment step or deadline distinct from the substantive grant/deny response. The seven-business-day (or 14) response under 47:1A-5(i)(1) is the sole required response; there is no statutory 'we received your request' acknowledgment clock.

Within my scope areas, no statutory clock or mandatory back-and-forth to cure a deficient request appears. The custodian may deny incomplete/overbroad requests (47:1A-5(f),(g)) but no fixed cure window is prescribed. Intake/clarification is primarily a sibling area; noted here only to record the absence of a cure deadline.

A broad mandatory redaction of email, medical, financial, birthdate, or general 'personal information' was proposed in earlier reprints of S2930 but was DELETED before enactment. Enacted 47:1A-5(a) mandates redaction only of SSN, credit card number, personal telephone number, driver license number, and covered-officer home addresses. Do not treat the broad PII list as an operative redaction rule.

A provision requiring denial of all requests by or for data brokers (and a data-broker registration/fee scheme) was in earlier reprints but was DELETED and NOT enacted. No data-broker processing rule exists in current OPRA.

P.L.2024, c.16, s.10 bars a non-subject who obtained a photo/video via OPRA from disclosing indecent/graphic images of intimate parts without consent (disorderly persons offense). Excluded from rules: it is a downstream use-restriction with a criminal penalty, not something the platform does differently while processing a request.

Beyond 'provide in the medium/format maintained' and 'convert if available without substantial IT manipulation' (47:1A-5(d)), OPRA states no ranked hierarchy of production formats the platform must apply.

OPRA creates no general fee waiver for indigent, non-profit, or public-interest requestors. The only statutory zero-fee cases are crime victims (NJ-M05) and records available on a public agency website (NJ-M04). Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

OPRA attaches fees only to copies/duplication; no fee is prescribed for mere inspection or examination during business hours (47:1A-5(a),(b)). No affirmative 'inspection is free' clause exists, so this is stated cautiously as an absence rather than an express rule.

No statutory provision imposes interest, late fees, or penalties on a requestor for unpaid or delayed OPRA fee payments; the only leverage is prepayment/deposit (NJ-M14, NJ-M15) and the 14-business-day record-retrieval window.

No numeric cap on cumulative special service charges (47:1A-5(c),(d)); charges are bounded only by 'reasonable / actual direct cost' with a rebuttable presumption of reasonableness (NJ-M06, NJ-M09, NJ-M10).
No statutory deadline governs completion of GRC mediation; mediation time is expressly excluded from the 90-day adjudication clock (NJ-M47), leaving mediation duration open-ended.
No bond or filing fee is required to appeal to the GRC (the statute affirmatively bars GRC fees, NJ-M45). No provision addresses a bond for Superior Court OPRA actions within OPRA itself.

structural_branches.description: NJ-A06: custodian identity forks by entity type - municipal clerk for a municipality vs. a formally designated officer for any other public agency - determining who must receive and answer the request.

NJ-A30/NJ-A31: a request landing on a non-custodian must be forwarded or redirected to the custodian, and is not deemed submitted (clock does not start) until the custodian receives it - a routing stage the engine must model before intake completes.

NJ-A32/NJ-A33: for records held only via remote access or courtesy copy from another (non-judicial-branch) agency, the request branches to a referral path - custodian directs the requestor to the originating agency within seven business days and the request is deemed completed.

NJ-A34: for records readily available in complete form on the agency website, the request branches to a self-service path - custodian may require retrieval from the website while providing locating directions - with downstream fulfillment/assist/physical-copy sub-branches (deferred to Deadlines/Fees).

NJ-A22/NJ-A23: requests branch on a mandatory legal-proceeding certification; a party to a proceeding is barred from OPRA for records subject to a court order/pending discovery, with a labor-organization/CBA-contractor carve-out - a gate the engine must evaluate before processing.
NJ-A24: requests that would substantially disrupt operations branch into a mandatory notify-and-negotiate-a-reasonable-solution stage before any denial is permitted.
Storage/archived records follow a distinct path: advise within 7/14 business days (NJ-T11), make available within 21 business days of advisement (NJ-T12), else deemed denied (NJ-T13).

Website-redirect fulfillment fork: redirect with directions (NJ-T31) -> deemed fulfilled after 7 business days or completeness carve-back (NJ-T32) -> good-faith assistance within 7 business days (NJ-T33) -> physical copy within 7 business days (NJ-T34).
Not-in-possession/courtesy-copy fork: custodian may decline and must redirect the requestor within 7 business days to the originating (non-judicial-branch) agency, completing the request (NJ-T16).
Declared-emergency fork suspending the (i)(1) and subsection-e deadlines, replaced by a reasonable-effort soft standard (NJ-T15).
Election-agency-specific processing: limited redaction (NJ-T41), 2-business-day immediate access (NJ-T42), election-eve noon deadlines (NJ-T43), website posting satisfies deadlines (NJ-T44).
Court protective-order path that can toll, limit, or eliminate the agency's duty to respond to a vexatious requestor (NJ-T46).
Daniel's Law path: OIP-approved covered-person home-address redaction (NJ-T36) with a 30-day agency compliance deadline (NJ-T38) and a triggered 14-business-day review window (NJ-T03).
Commercial requestor may elect 7-business-day delivery instead of the default 14, for up to 2x production cost (NJ-T06).

A denied requestor must elect one of two mutually exclusive review paths within 45 days: an action in Superior Court before a designated judge, OR a complaint to the Government Records Council ('in lieu of' filing in Superior Court). NJ-M28 / NJ-M29.

Certification of 'commercial purpose' forks the request into a distinct track: a 14-business-day response window (vs 7), an optional 2x expedite fee, and miscertification-penalty exposure. NJ-M13 / NJ-M12 / NJ-M55.

Custodian silence past the 7/14-business-day window converts the request to a constructive denial (terminal state opening the 45-day appeal clock), unless the requestor withheld accurate identity/contact info, which pauses the obligation. NJ-M25 / NJ-M26.
A record in storage/archive routes to a separate timeline: advise within 7/14 days, produce within no more than 21 business days, else deemed denied. NJ-M27.

GRC processing is a staged pipeline: mediation offer -> (on decline/failure) investigation and frivolous/jurisdiction screen -> agency response -> APA contested-case hearing if accessibility cannot be decided on the papers -> majority-vote decision. NJ-M39 through NJ-M44.

An agency may open a separate Superior Court track (verified complaint, clear-and-convincing standard) to obtain a protective order that limits or eliminates its future duty to respond to a requestor found to intend substantial interruption of government function, subject to a labor-organization carve-out. NJ-M58 / NJ-M59 / NJ-M60 / NJ-M61.
A request that would substantially disrupt agency operations routes to a mandatory notice-and-negotiation step before the custodian may deny access. NJ-M21.

rules.legal_concept: Right of every person to access public records
rules.atomic_rule: Every person has the right to inspect, copy, or receive a copy of any public record maintained or kept on file by any public agency (subject to statutory exemptions).
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right of any person)
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by any federal law or state statute, all records maintained or kept on file by any public agency, whether or not such records are required by any law or by any rule or regulation, shall be public records and every person shall have the right to (1) inspect such records promptly during regular office or business hours, (2) copy such records in accordance with subsection (g) of section 1-212, or (3) receive a copy of such records in accordance with section 1-212.
rules.notes: Universal-access rule per shared eligibility key. 'Person' defined broadly (CT-0004); statute imposes no residency or purpose condition.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement to request records
rules.atomic_rule: Access is granted to 'every person' / 'any person' with no in-state residency condition; a requester need not be a Connecticut resident.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: all records maintained or kept on file by any public agency ... shall be public records and every person shall have the right to (1) inspect such records promptly during regular office or business hours
rules.notes: Emitted as a rule with the shared key (not a material negative) per universal-access symmetry. The right runs to 'every person' with no residency qualifier anywhere in Chapter 14.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state or justify a purpose to inspect, copy, or receive public records; the right is unconditional as to motive.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: every person shall have the right to (1) inspect such records promptly during regular office or business hours, (2) copy such records in accordance with subsection (g) of section 1-212, or (3) receive a copy of such records in accordance with section 1-212.
rules.notes: Shared-key rule per universal-access symmetry. Chapter 14 attaches no purpose/use condition to the right of access.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'person'
rules.atomic_rule: 'Person' who may request records includes natural persons and enumerated organizational entities.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: 'Person' means natural person, partnership, corporation, limited liability company, association or society.
rules.notes: Definition the platform branches on for who qualifies as a requester; entities as well as individuals may request.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'public agency' (municipal coverage)
rules.atomic_rule: 'Public agency' subject to FOIA includes any office, department, board, commission, authority or official of any city, town, borough, municipal corporation, school district or other political subdivision, plus functional-equivalent private entities.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: 'Public agency' or 'agency' means: (A) Any executive, administrative or legislative office of the state or any political subdivision of the state and any state or town agency, any department, institution, bureau, board, commission, authority or official of the state or of any city, town, borough, municipal corporation, school district, regional district or other district or other political subdivision of the state ...; (B) Any person to the extent such person is deemed to be the functional equivalent of a public agency pursuant to law; or (C) Any 'implementing agency', as defined in section 32-222.
rules.notes: Confirms municipal coverage. Functional-equivalent clause (B) can pull a private contractor into coverage - a coverage branch the engine may need to classify.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'public records or files'
rules.atomic_rule: A 'public record' is any recorded data or information relating to the conduct of the public's business prepared, owned, used, received or retained by a public agency (or which the agency is entitled to receive by law/contract), in any medium.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: 'Public records or files' means any recorded data or information relating to the conduct of the public's business prepared, owned, used, received or retained by a public agency, or to which a public agency is entitled to receive a copy by law or contract under section 1-218, whether such data or information be handwritten, typed, tape-recorded, videotaped, printed, photostated, photographed or recorded by any other method.
rules.notes: Defines the object of a request; format-neutral. Software branches on whether a requested item is a 'public record'.

rules.legal_concept: Written application required to receive a copy
rules.atomic_rule: To receive a copy of a public record, the requester must apply in writing; an oral request for a copy is not enforceable before the FOI Commission.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks a copy (as opposed to inspection)
rules.source_language: Any person applying in writing shall receive, promptly upon request, a plain, facsimile, electronic or certified copy of any public record.
rules.notes: Case law (130 CA 448) holds the writing requirement makes copy requests enforceable and that promptness was not violated by failing to honor oral copy requests. Note contrast: the right to INSPECT under 1-210(a) carries no writing requirement.

rules.legal_concept: Prompt inspection during business hours
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency must permit inspection of public records promptly during regular office or business hours.
rules.trigger: Request to inspect public records
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly" from request during regular office/business hours
rules.source_language: every person shall have the right to (1) inspect such records promptly during regular office or business hours
rules.notes: Soft standard - no fixed day-count. Case law (116 CA 171) held a flat two-week limit imposed 'without any explanation or reason' was an arbitrary limitation and abuse of discretion; promptness is fact-specific.

rules.legal_concept: Prompt provision of copies
rules.atomic_rule: Upon a written request, a public agency must provide the requested copy of a public record promptly.
rules.trigger: Written request for a copy
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly upon request" from written request
rules.source_language: Any person applying in writing shall receive, promptly upon request, a plain, facsimile, electronic or certified copy of any public record.
rules.notes: Soft standard - no numeric deadline. Distinct from the 4-business-day denial deadline (CT-0012), which governs only denials.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must issue from the custodian/official with custody or control
rules.atomic_rule: Any denial of access must be made by the public agency official who has custody or control of the public record.
rules.trigger: Agency denies inspection or copying
rules.source_language: Any denial of the right to inspect or copy records provided for under section 1-210 shall be made to the person requesting such right by the public agency official who has custody or control of the public record, in writing, within four business days of such request
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: custodian designation drives routing (who must issue the response).

rules.legal_concept: Records kept accessible; default custodial location
rules.atomic_rule: An agency must keep public records at its regular office in an accessible place; if it has no such office, the records are kept with the clerk of the political subdivision or the Secretary of the State.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Each such agency shall keep and maintain all public records in its custody at its regular office or place of business in an accessible place and, if there is no such office or place of business, the public records pertaining to such agency shall be kept in the office of the clerk of the political subdivision in which such public agency is located or of the Secretary of the State, as the case may be.
rules.notes: Included for the routing sliver (default location a requester is directed to when an agency has no office), not as a general recordkeeping mandate.

rules.legal_concept: Written denial within four business days
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency must issue any denial of inspection/copying to the requester in writing within four business days of the request.
rules.trigger: Request that the agency will deny
rules.clock_spec: 4 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: Any denial of the right to inspect or copy records provided for under section 1-210 shall be made to the person requesting such right by the public agency official who has custody or control of the public record, in writing, within four business days of such request
rules.notes: This is the only fixed statutory response window in CT FOIA, and it applies specifically to denials (not to grants, which are governed by 'promptly').

rules.legal_concept: Ten-business-day denial window for personnel/medical-file requests
rules.atomic_rule: When a request is subject to the personnel/medical-file objection process (1-214(b)-(c)), any denial must be made in writing within ten business days of the request.
rules.trigger: Request determined subject to 1-214(b) and (c) (personnel/medical/similar files)
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: except when the request is determined to be subject to subsections (b) and (c) of section 1-214, in which case such denial shall be made, in writing, within ten business days of such request.
rules.notes: Same concept as CT-0012 but a longer window for the personnel-file branch, to accommodate the employee-objection process.

rules.legal_concept: Failure to comply within the applicable window deemed a denial
rules.atomic_rule: An agency's failure to comply with an inspection/copy request within the applicable number of business days is deemed a denial (which then starts the appeal clock).
rules.trigger: Applicable business-day window (4 or 10) elapses without compliance
rules.clock_spec: deemed denial upon expiry of 4 business-days (or 10 for personnel/medical) from request
rules.source_language: Failure to comply with a request to so inspect or copy such public record within the applicable number of business days shall be deemed to be a denial.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: constructive/deemed-denial trigger (silence = denial). Terminal event that opens the 30-day FOIC appeal window (CT-0033). Section 1-214(c) similarly deems failure to comply a denial for personnel-file requests.

rules.legal_concept: Per-page copy fee ceiling - municipal and other agencies
rules.atomic_rule: For all public agencies other than state offices/agencies, the fee for a copy of a public record shall not exceed fifty cents per page.
rules.trigger: Requester receives a copy from a non-state public agency
rules.source_language: (B) By all other public agencies, as defined in section 1-200, shall not exceed fifty cents per page.
rules.notes: Municipal/local rate. Ceiling: the city may set any per-page fee at or below $0.50. 'Page' means one side of a piece of printed matter (108 CA 471).

rules.legal_concept: Per-page copy fee ceiling - state offices/agencies
rules.atomic_rule: For state executive/administrative/legislative offices and state agencies (and judicial offices in their administrative functions), the copy fee shall not exceed twenty-five cents per page.
rules.trigger: Requester receives a copy from a state office/agency
rules.source_language: (A) By an executive, administrative or legislative office of the state, a state agency or a department, institution, bureau, board, commission, authority or official of the state, including a committee of, or created by, such an office ..., and also including any judicial office, official or body or committee thereof but only in respect to its or their administrative functions, shall not exceed twenty-five cents per page
rules.notes: Same concept as CT-0015 with a different ceiling for state agencies; do not merge the values - the constraint differs by agency class.

rules.legal_concept: Transcription fee limited to cost
rules.atomic_rule: Where a copy requires a transcription, or a person requests a transcription of a public record, the transcription fee shall not exceed the agency's cost.
rules.trigger: Copy requires, or requester applies for, a transcription
rules.source_language: If any copy provided in accordance with said Freedom of Information Act requires a transcription, or if any person applies for a transcription of a public record, the fee for such transcription shall not exceed the cost thereof to the public agency.
rules.notes: Ceiling = actual cost to the agency; no fixed number stated.

rules.legal_concept: Fee for computer-stored records limited to cost with enumerated components
rules.atomic_rule: The fee for a copy of computer-stored public records shall not exceed the agency's cost, and (for non-preexisting printouts) may include only enumerated components: employee hourly salary for producing/formatting/programming (not search/retrieval except sub-(4)), outside copying-service cost, actual storage-media cost, and certain computer-time charges.
rules.trigger: Request for a copy of computer-stored public records
rules.source_language: The fee for any copy provided in accordance with subsection (a) of section 1-211 shall not exceed the cost thereof to the public agency. In determining such costs for a copy, other than for a printout which exists at the time that the agency responds to the request for such copy, an agency may include only: (1) An amount equal to the hourly salary attributed to all agency employees engaged in providing the requested computer-stored public record ... but not including search or retrieval costs except as provided in subdivision (4) of this subsection; (2) An amount equal to the cost to the agency of engaging an outside professional electronic copying service ...; (3) The actual cost of the storage devices or media provided ...; and (4) The computer time charges incurred by the agency ... where another agency or contractor provides the agency with computer storage and retrieval services.
rules.notes: Ceiling = cost, with a closed list of includable components. Notably excludes search/retrieval labor except sub-(4). DAS issues guidelines for consistency. Kept in one row (closed enumerated list, not a bundle of independent duties).

rules.legal_concept: Registered-voter name copy fee cap
rules.atomic_rule: The fee for a copy of the names of registered voters shall not exceed three cents per name delivered, or the agency's cost, whichever is less.
rules.trigger: Request for a copy of registered-voter names
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, the fee for any copy of the names of registered voters shall not exceed three cents per name delivered or the cost thereof to the public agency, as determined pursuant to this subsection, whichever is less.
rules.notes: Record-specific fee ceiling ($0.03/name or cost, lesser). Relevant to municipal registrars.

rules.legal_concept: Certification fee
rules.atomic_rule: For certifying a copy of records/files (or certifying a fact appearing therein), the fee is one dollar for the first page and fifty cents for each additional page.
rules.trigger: Requester asks the custodian to certify a copy or fact
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law, the fee for any person who has the custody of any public records or files for certifying any copy of such records or files, or certifying to any fact appearing therefrom, shall be for the first page of such certificate, or copy and certificate, one dollar; and for each additional page, fifty cents.
rules.notes: Fixed statewide amount ('except as otherwise provided by law'). Separate from and additive to the per-page copy fee.

rules.legal_concept: Hand-held scanner copying fee cap
rules.atomic_rule: An individual may copy a public record with a hand-held scanner; the agency may establish a fee not to exceed twenty dollars per scanning session.
rules.trigger: Individual copies records on-site with a hand-held scanner
rules.source_language: Any individual may copy a public record through the use of a hand-held scanner. A public agency may establish a fee structure not to exceed twenty dollars for an individual to pay each time the individual copies records at the agency with a hand-held scanner.
rules.notes: Ceiling $20/session. 'Hand-held scanner' means a battery-operated device leaving no mark and not unreasonably interfering (statutory definition); a flatbed scanner does not qualify (135 CA 202).

rules.legal_concept: Prepayment permitted when fee estimated at $10 or more
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency may require prepayment of any fee if the fee is estimated to be ten dollars or more.
rules.trigger: Estimated fee is $10 or more
rules.source_language: A public agency may require the prepayment of any fee required or permitted under the Freedom of Information Act if such fee is estimated to be ten dollars or more.
rules.notes: Discretionary. $10 is the floor at/above which prepayment may be demanded; the city sets whether/how it invokes it.

rules.legal_concept: No sales tax on FOIA fees
rules.atomic_rule: Sales tax shall not be imposed on any transaction for which a fee is required or permissible under the copy-fee statute (or § 1-227).
rules.trigger: Collection of an FOIA copy/records fee
rules.source_language: The sales tax provided in chapter 219 shall not be imposed upon any transaction for which a fee is required or permissible under this section or section 1-227.
rules.notes: Affects the computed charge (no tax component); fixed at zero tax.

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory fee waiver
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency shall waive any copy fee when any enumerated ground applies: requester is indigent; records are exempt under 1-210(b); compliance benefits the general welfare in the agency's judgment; requester is an elected official of the political subdivision certifying the record pertains to official duties; or requester is Public Defender Services personnel/appointed counsel certifying the record pertains to their duties.
rules.trigger: Any one of five enumerated waiver conditions is met
rules.source_language: The public agency shall waive any fee provided for in this section when: (1) The person requesting the records is an indigent individual; (2) The records located are determined by the public agency to be exempt from disclosure under subsection (b) of section 1-210; (3) In its judgment, compliance with the applicant's request benefits the general welfare; (4) The person requesting the record is an elected official of a political subdivision of the state and the official (A) obtains the record from an agency of the political subdivision in which the official serves, and (B) certifies that the record pertains to the official's duties; or (5) The person requesting the records is a member of the Division of Public Defender Services or an attorney appointed by the court as a Division of Public Defender Services assigned counsel under section 51-296 and such member or attorney certifies that the record pertains to the member's or attorney's duties.
rules.notes: Kept as one row (single 'shall waive' duty with disjunctive grounds). Mandatory ('shall'); ground (3) 'general welfare' rests on agency judgment.

rules.legal_concept: Agency discretion over type of copy
rules.atomic_rule: The type of copy provided (plain, facsimile, electronic, or certified) is within the public agency's discretion, subject to the two exceptions in CT-0026 and CT-0027.
rules.trigger: Written request for a copy
