rules.source_language: The type of copy provided shall be within the discretion of the public agency, except (1) the agency shall provide a certified copy whenever requested, and (2) if the applicant does not have access to a computer or facsimile machine, the public agency shall not send the applicant an electronic or facsimile copy.
rules.notes: General discretion rule; the two carve-outs are split into CT-0026/CT-0027. Cross-references electronic-format duty for computer records (CT-0028).

rules.legal_concept: Certified copy on demand
rules.atomic_rule: The agency shall provide a certified copy whenever a certified copy is requested.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for a certified copy
rules.source_language: except (1) the agency shall provide a certified copy whenever requested
rules.notes: Certification carries the separate fee in CT-0020. 'Certified' requires a written attestation as a true copy by an authorized official (108 CA 471).

rules.legal_concept: No electronic/fax copy when requester lacks access
rules.atomic_rule: If the applicant does not have access to a computer or facsimile machine, the agency shall not send an electronic or facsimile copy.
rules.trigger: Applicant lacks access to a computer or facsimile machine
rules.source_language: and (2) if the applicant does not have access to a computer or facsimile machine, the public agency shall not send the applicant an electronic or facsimile copy.
rules.notes: Constrains the format the agency may deliver based on requester's access.

rules.legal_concept: Computer-stored records provided in requested medium
rules.atomic_rule: An agency maintaining public records in a computer storage system shall provide a copy of nonexempt data in the medium the requester specifies (paper, disk, tape, other electronic medium, or email), if the agency can reasonably make or have such copy made.
rules.trigger: Request for computer-stored nonexempt data, format specified
rules.source_language: Any public agency which maintains public records in a computer storage system shall provide, to any person making a request pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, a copy of any nonexempt data contained in such records, properly identified, on paper, disk, tape or any other electronic storage device or medium requested by the person, including an electronic copy sent to the electronic mail address of the person making such request, if the agency can reasonably make any such copy or have any such copy made.
rules.notes: Duty conditioned on 'reasonably' being able to make the copy - a soft feasibility standard. Fee governed by CT-0018.

rules.legal_concept: Notice to employees when disclosure believed to invade privacy
rules.atomic_rule: When an agency receives a request for records in an employee's personnel/medical/similar file and reasonably believes disclosure would legally constitute an invasion of privacy, it shall immediately notify in writing each employee concerned and their collective-bargaining representative.
rules.trigger: Request for personnel/medical/similar file where agency reasonably believes disclosure would invade privacy
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "immediately" notify from receipt of request
rules.source_language: Whenever a public agency receives a request to inspect or copy records contained in any of its employees' personnel or medical files and similar files, and the agency reasonably believes that the disclosure of such records would legally constitute an invasion of privacy, the agency shall immediately notify in writing (A) each employee concerned, provided such notice shall not be required to be in writing where impractical due to the large number of employees concerned, and (B) the collective bargaining representative, if any, of each employee concerned.
rules.notes: Starts the objection process (CT-0031). 'Immediately' is a soft standard. Notice may be non-written where impractical due to large employee numbers.

rules.legal_concept: Disclose then notify when no invasion believed
rules.atomic_rule: When an agency receives a personnel/medical-file request and reasonably believes disclosure would NOT invade privacy, it shall first disclose the records, then within a reasonable time make a reasonable attempt to send the employee(s) and their bargaining representative a copy or brief description of the request.
rules.trigger: Request for personnel/medical file where agency reasonably believes disclosure would not invade privacy
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "within a reasonable time after such disclosure" for post-disclosure notice
rules.source_language: Whenever a public agency receives a request to inspect or copy records contained in any of its employees' personnel or medical files and similar files, and the agency reasonably believes that the disclosure of such records would not legally constitute an invasion of privacy, the agency shall first disclose the requested records to the person making the request ... and subsequently, within a reasonable time after such disclosure, make a reasonable attempt to send a written or an electronic copy of the request ... or a brief description of such request, to each employee concerned and the collective bargaining representative, if any, of each employee concerned.
rules.notes: Alternative branch: no pre-disclosure hold; disclosure precedes notice. Added by P.A. 18-93.

rules.legal_concept: Employee objection window before disclosure
rules.atomic_rule: After giving privacy notice, the agency shall disclose the requested records unless the employee or their bargaining representative files a written objection within seven business days from receipt of the notice (or, absent evidence of receipt, within nine business days from when the notice was mailed/sent/posted/given).
rules.trigger: Privacy notice given under 1-214(b)(1)
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from employee receipt of notice; or 9 business-days from mailing/sending if no evidence of receipt
rules.source_language: A public agency which has provided notice under subdivision (1) of subsection (b) of this section shall disclose the records requested unless it receives a written objection from the employee concerned or the employee's collective bargaining representative, if any, within seven business days from the receipt by the employee or such collective bargaining representative of the notice or, if there is no evidence of receipt of written notice, not later than nine business days from the date the notice is actually mailed, sent, posted or otherwise given.
rules.notes: Kept as one row (single objection window with a receipt-based primary and a mailing-based fallback). Objection must be on an agency form, signed under penalty of false statement.

rules.legal_concept: Records withheld once objection filed until FOIC order
rules.atomic_rule: Upon the filing of a valid employee/representative objection, the agency shall not disclose the requested records unless ordered to do so by the Freedom of Information Commission; failure to comply with the request is itself a denial for appeal purposes.
rules.trigger: Written objection filed under 1-214(c)
rules.clock_spec: request enters withheld/hold state pending FOIC order under § 1-206
rules.source_language: Upon the filing of an objection as provided in this subsection, the agency shall not disclose the requested records unless ordered to do so by the Freedom of Information Commission pursuant to section 1-206. Failure to comply with a request to inspect or copy records under this section shall constitute a denial for the purposes of section 1-206.
rules.notes: Request enters a hold state pending FOIC resolution; the employee may later approve disclosure in writing even after a representative objects. This is a state-specific processing branch.

rules.legal_concept: Appeal to FOI Commission within thirty days of denial
rules.atomic_rule: A person denied access (or any FOIA right) may appeal to the Freedom of Information Commission by filing a notice of appeal not later than thirty days after the denial.
rules.trigger: Denial of access or other FOIA right (including a deemed denial)
rules.clock_spec: 30 calendar-days from the denial
rules.source_language: Any person denied the right to inspect or copy records under section 1-210 or wrongfully denied the right to attend any meeting of a public agency or denied any other right conferred by the Freedom of Information Act may appeal therefrom to the Freedom of Information Commission, by filing a notice of appeal with said commission. A notice of appeal shall be filed not later than thirty days after such denial, except in the case of an unnoticed or secret meeting, in which case the appeal shall be filed not later than thirty days after the person filing the appeal receives actual or constructive notice that such meeting was held.
rules.notes: Administrative-appeal stage (namespaced appeal.administrative). Runs from denial, including a constructive denial (CT-0014).

rules.legal_concept: When a notice of appeal is deemed filed
rules.atomic_rule: A notice of appeal is deemed filed on the date the commission receives it, or on the postmark date if received more than thirty days after the denial.
rules.trigger: Notice of appeal transmitted to the commission
rules.source_language: For purposes of this subsection, such notice of appeal shall be deemed to be filed on the date it is received by said commission or on the date it is postmarked, if received more than thirty days after the date of the denial from which such appeal is taken.
rules.notes: Mailbox-style rule fixing the filing date used to test the 30-day deadline (CT-0033).

rules.legal_concept: Commission must hear and decide within one year
rules.atomic_rule: The Freedom of Information Commission shall, after due notice, hear and decide the appeal not later than one year after the filing of the notice of appeal.
rules.trigger: Notice of appeal filed with the commission
rules.clock_spec: 1 year from filing of notice of appeal
rules.source_language: Said commission shall, after due notice to the parties, hear and decide the appeal not later than one year after the filing of the notice of appeal.
rules.notes: General adjudication deadline for the commission; the expedited/privileged track (CT-0036) has shorter windows.

rules.legal_concept: Privileged (expedited) appeal hearing and decision windows
rules.atomic_rule: For appeals the commission's regulations designate as privileged, the appeal shall be heard not later than thirty days after receipt of the notice of appeal and decided not later than sixty days after the hearing.
rules.trigger: Appeal designated privileged under commission regulations
rules.clock_spec: hearing within 30 days of notice receipt; decision within 60 days after the hearing
rules.source_language: The commission shall adopt regulations in accordance with chapter 54, establishing criteria for those appeals which shall be privileged in their assignment for hearing. Any such appeal shall be heard not later than thirty days after receipt of a notice of appeal and decided not later than sixty days after the hearing.
rules.notes: Expedited track; criteria set by commission regulation. Distinct from the executive-session preliminary-hearing 72-hour track (also in 1-206(b)(1), records-processing-marginal).

rules.legal_concept: Judicial appeal of a commission decision
rules.atomic_rule: A party aggrieved by a decision of the Freedom of Information Commission may appeal to the Superior Court in accordance with the Uniform Administrative Procedure Act (§ 4-183).
rules.trigger: Aggrievement by a final FOIC decision
rules.source_language: Any party aggrieved by the decision of said commission may appeal therefrom, in accordance with the provisions of section 4-183.
rules.notes: Namespaced appeal.judicial (court review), distinct from the internal FOIC stage. The 45-day filing deadline and mechanics live in UAPA § 4-183, outside Chapter 14 - flag for a UAPA cross-reference pass.

rules.legal_concept: Relief from a vexatious requester
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency may petition the FOI Commission for relief from a vexatious requester; upon granting the petition the commission may order that the agency need not comply with future requests from that requester for a specified period not exceeding one year.
rules.trigger: Agency alleges a requester is vexatious (sworn petition detailing history)
rules.clock_spec: relief period not to exceed one year during which future requests need not be processed
rules.source_language: Upon a grant of such petition, the commission may provide appropriate relief commensurate with the vexatious conduct, including, but not limited to, an order that the agency need not comply with future requests from the vexatious requester for a specified period of time, but not to exceed one year.
rules.notes: Classification/routing branch that can block processing of a requester's future requests. Requires a sworn petition and commission adjudication (petition decided within one year of filing).

rules.legal_concept: Inmate request - notice to Commissioner before compliance
rules.atomic_rule: When an agency receives a records request from a person confined in a correctional or Whiting Forensic Hospital facility, it shall promptly notify the Commissioner of Correction (or Commissioner of Mental Health and Addiction Services) before complying, and the commissioner may withhold a record believed exempt under 1-210(b)(18).
rules.trigger: Request from a person confined in a correctional institution/facility or Whiting Forensic Hospital facility
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly notify" the commissioner before complying
rules.source_language: Whenever a public agency receives a request from any person confined in a correctional institution or facility or a Whiting Forensic Hospital facility, for disclosure of any public record under the Freedom of Information Act, the public agency shall promptly notify the Commissioner of Correction or the Commissioner of Mental Health and Addiction Services in the case of a person confined in a Whiting Forensic Hospital facility of such request, in the manner prescribed by the commissioner, before complying with the request as required by the Freedom of Information Act.
rules.notes: Requester-classification routing branch that inserts an external-review step before disclosure. Applies to any public agency, including municipal, that receives an inmate request.

rules.legal_concept: Security-record request - notice to Commissioner before compliance
rules.atomic_rule: When an agency (other than Judicial/Legislative) receives a request for records described in 1-210(b)(19) (security/emergency-response records), it shall promptly notify the Commissioner of Administrative Services or Emergency Services and Public Protection before complying; the commissioner may direct the agency to withhold, and any appeal runs against the chief executive officer who issued the withholding directive.
rules.trigger: Request for records described in § 1-210(b)(19)
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly notify" the commissioner before complying
rules.source_language: Whenever a public agency, except the Judicial Department or Legislative Department, receives a request from any person for disclosure of any records described in subdivision (19) of subsection (b) of this section under the Freedom of Information Act, the public agency shall promptly notify the Commissioner of Administrative Services or the Commissioner of Emergency Services and Public Protection, as applicable, of such request, in the manner prescribed by such commissioner, before complying with the request as required by the Freedom of Information Act.
rules.notes: Record-type routing branch inserting external review before disclosure and redirecting the respondent for appeal purposes (against the CEO issuing the directive). Applies to municipal/district/regional agencies.

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory redaction of protected residential addresses
rules.atomic_rule: When an agency receives a request that specifically names a person who has filed a confidentiality request for their residential address, the agency shall copy the record and redact that person's residential address before disclosing it (reasonable-effort redaction for list-type requests).
rules.trigger: Request naming/covering a person who filed an address-confidentiality request under § 1-217
rules.source_language: Any public agency that receives a request for a record subject to disclosure under this chapter where such request (A) specifically names a person who has requested that his or her address be kept confidential under subdivision (1) of this subsection, shall make a copy of the record requested to be disclosed and shall redact the copy to remove such person's residential address prior to disclosing such record, (B) is for an existing list that is derived from a readily accessible electronic database, shall make a reasonable effort to redact the residential address ... prior to the release of such list, or (C) is for any list that the public agency voluntarily creates in response to a request for disclosure, shall make a reasonable effort to redact the residential address ... prior to the release of such list.
rules.notes: Creates a redaction workflow triggered by the request. Protected classes (police officers, judges, prosecutors, DCF/correction/parole staff, etc.) are enumerated in 1-217(a)(1). Does not apply to documents/lists exempted by 1-217(e).

rules.legal_concept: Segregation of nonexempt from exempt data (judicial rule)
rules.atomic_rule: When a request encompasses both exempt and nonexempt data, disclosure of the nonexempt portion may be ordered where the agency can reasonably separate the data, but only after inquiry into reasonable separability and (for computerized data) a public-safety assessment.
rules.trigger: Request incorporating both exempt and nonexempt data
rules.source_language: Section does not empower commission to order agency to separate exempt from non-exempt data when request incorporates both and no inquiry is made into whether agency can reasonably separate such data or whether non-exempt data alone would satisfy requester.
rules.source_authority: Director of Info. Tech. v. FOIC, 307 Conn. 648 (2012) (construing Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-211)
rules.notes: Judicially established. Connecticut FOIA has NO general statutory segregability clause; segregability is governed by this holding (and by 323 Conn. 1 for redacting privileged matter). Quoted language is the official statutory annotation summarizing the holding - verify against the full opinion (318/323/307 Conn.) in a case-law pass. Rule_type secondary: Presumption.

structural_branches.description: Personnel/medical-file request enters a hold state once an employee or bargaining representative files an objection; agency cannot disclose until FOIC orders it (§ 1-214(c)).
Privacy-invasion branch: agency must notify affected employees and unions and pause disclosure pending the objection window (§ 1-214(b)(1)).
No-invasion branch: agency discloses first, then notifies employees within a reasonable time (§ 1-214(b)(2)).
FOIC may relieve an agency from processing a requester's future requests for up to one year on a vexatious-requester petition (§ 1-206(b)(6)).
Inmate/confined-person requests are routed to the Commissioner of Correction (or DMHAS) for exemption review before compliance (§ 1-210(c)).
Requests for § 1-210(b)(19) security records are routed to DAS/DESPP for withholding directive, redirecting who the appeal runs against (§ 1-210(d)).
Privileged appeals follow an expedited 30-day-hearing / 60-day-decision track distinct from the general one-year track (§ 1-206(b)(1)).
Court-review path for FOIC decisions via UAPA § 4-183, distinct from the internal FOIC appeal stage (§ 1-206(d)).
Non-response within the applicable business-day window converts the request into a deemed denial, opening the appeal path (§ 1-206(a)).
A request naming a person with a confidential-address filing forces a redaction step before disclosure (§ 1-217(a)(2)).

material_negatives.note: Connecticut FOIA sets NO general acknowledgment/response deadline for granting access. The only fixed statutory window is the four-business-day (ten for personnel/medical) deadline to issue a DENIAL (§ 1-206(a)); grants are governed only by the soft 'promptly' standard (§§ 1-210(a), 1-212(a)). Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

No statutory provision requires or authorizes a clarification/narrowing round-trip with a tolling clock. CT law is silent; agencies handle vague requests case-by-case (and may pursue vexatious-requester relief under § 1-206(b)(6)).
Connecticut FOIA draws no commercial-vs-noncommercial fee distinction and defines no 'commercial purpose'. Copy fees are the same per-page/cost ceilings regardless of requester purpose (§ 1-212).

No statute authorizes a separate search or staff-time fee for PAPER copies; the charge is per-page only (§ 1-212(a)). For computer-stored records, staff time for producing/formatting may be included but search/retrieval costs are expressly excluded except limited third-party computer-time charges (§ 1-212(b)).

Chapter 14 contains no express 'adequate/reasonable search' standard governing how an agency must search for responsive records; the obligation is implied through the access right and FOIC adjudication rather than a codified processing rule.

No statute prescribes a required submission channel or a mandatory request form for records requests generally; only that a request for a COPY be in writing (§ 1-212(a)). Inspection carries no writing requirement.

Section 1-206(a) requires a denial to be 'in writing' within the deadline but does not, on its face, require the agency to state the statutory basis/reason for the denial; any reason-statement obligation arises in FOIC practice rather than the statute.

No statute imposes an automatic litigation/preservation hold triggered by a records request or a pending FOIC appeal; retention is governed by separate records-management law (Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 11-8 et seq.), outside Chapter 14's request-processing rules.
